papers.title_zh: 奥希替尼联合赛沃替尼对比铂类-培美曲塞治疗奥希替尼进展后MET过表达或扩增的EGFR突变晚期NSCLC：III期随机试验显示无进展生存与总生存显著延长
papers.title_en: Osimertinib-Savolitinib in Advanced NSCLC after Progression during EGFR-TKI Therapy.
papers.authors: Lu S, Girard N, Yang JC, Shepherd FA, Dong X, Arulananda S, Metro G, Hayashi H et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Medical Oncology, Shanghai Chest Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, School of Medicine, Shanghai.
papers.results: 主要终点PFS（盲法独立中心评估）：疾病进展或死亡HR 0.55（95%CI 0.42–0.72），P<0.001；OS：死亡HR 0.68（95%CI 0.50–0.91），P=0.01（最终分析）；12个月PFS率36% vs 10%，12个月OS率70% vs 53%；治疗期间最常见不良事件为外周水肿（49%）、贫血（26%）、腹泻（26%）；≥3级不良事件64% vs 63%
papers.authors_conclusion: 在奥希替尼治疗期间进展、伴MET过表达或MET扩增或两者兼有的EGFR突变局部晚期或转移性NSCLC患者中，奥希替尼-赛沃替尼较铂类-培美曲塞显著延长无进展生存和总生存（由阿斯利康资助；SAFFRON，NCT05261399）
papers.ai_note: 开放标签设计，PFS依赖盲法独立中心评估以部分抵消偏倚，但症状性毒性（外周水肿49%）可能影响治疗中止与后续治疗；OS为最终分析且阳性，摘要未交代交叉用药、后续治疗分布及多重性检验策略对OS解释的影响；人群经严格生物标志物限定（IHC 3+≥90%或FISH ≥10拷贝），筛查1746例仅随机338例，结论外推至其他MET定义（如低水平扩增、蛋白中等表达）需谨慎；对照组为化疗，未设奥希替尼+安慰剂臂，故不能区分赛沃替尼的增量贡献；摘要未报告客观缓解率、缓解持续时间及PFS2等次要终点。

pico.p: EGFR突变、局部晚期或转移性NSCLC，伴MET过表达（IHC 3+且≥90%肿瘤细胞）或MET扩增（FISH ≥10基因拷贝）或两者兼有，且在奥希替尼治疗期间进展；筛查1746例，随机338例（奥希替尼-赛沃替尼组171例，铂类-培美曲塞组167例）
pico.ic: 奥希替尼80 mg每日一次联合赛沃替尼300 mg每日两次 vs 静脉铂类-培美曲塞化疗

papers.reason: 为EGFR-TKI耐药后MET驱动耐药这一常见临床困境确立了一个III期级别的联合靶向方案，直接改变奥希替尼进展后伴MET过表达/扩增患者的治疗选择与耐药再活检（MET IHC/FISH）的临床路径，并为后续MET-TKI联合研究提供对照基线。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Savolitinib is an oral, potent, highly selective MET-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). Combination therapy with savolitinib and osimertinib, an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-TKI, has shown activity in patients with EGFR-mutated, advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both, after progression during EGFR-TKI therapy. METHODS: In this international, phase 3, open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression (staining intensity of 3+ for MET in ≥90% of tumor cells on immunohistochemical analysis), MET amplification (≥10 gene copies on fluorescence in situ hybridization), or both whose disease had progressed during osimertinib therapy to receive osimertinib (at a dose of 80 mg once daily) plus savolitinib (300 mg twice daily) or intravenous platinum-pemetrexed. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival and safety. RESULTS: Of the 1746 patients screened, 338 were randomly assigned to receive osimertinib-savolitinib (171 patients) or platinum-pemetrexed (167 patients). Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free survival than platinum-pemetrexed (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.55; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.72; P<0.001), as well as significantly longer overall survival (hazard ratio for death, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.50 to 0.91; P = 0.01; final analysis). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of 12-month progression-free survival was 36% in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and 10% in the platinum-pemetrexed group, and the estimate of 12-month overall survival was 70% and 53%, respectively. The most frequently reported adverse events that occurred during treatment in the osimertinib-savolitinib group were peripheral edema (in 49% of the patients), anemia (in 26%), and diarrhea (in 26%). Grade 3 or higher adverse events during treatment were reported in 64% of the patients in the osimertinib-savolitinib group and in 63% of those in the platinum-pemetrexed group. CONCLUSIONS: Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than platinum-pemetrexed among patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both that had progressed during osimertinib therapy (Funded by AstraZeneca; SAFFRON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05261399.).

papers.title_zh: Dalmelitinib联合Aumolertinib对比铂类化疗治疗EGFR-TKI耐药后MET扩增晚期NSCLC的随机III期试验：PFS显著改善
papers.title_en: Dalmelitinib Plus Aumolertinib in Advanced NSCLC Patients With EGFR-TKI Resistance and MET Amplification: A Randomized Phase 3 Trial.
papers.authors: Li Z, Dong X, Yu Y, Yao W, Luo Y, Meng X, Yu X, Hu J et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Medical Oncology, Shanghai Chest Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, School of Medicine, Shanghai, Ch…
papers.results: 中位随访11.2个月；中位PFS为6.2个月 vs 4.4个月（HR 0.60；95%CI 0.45-0.81；P<0.001）；ORR为59.6% vs 38.6%；中位DoR为9.7个月 vs 4.4个月；OS数据未成熟；≥3级治疗相关不良事件为50.0% vs 51.0%
papers.authors_conclusion: dalmelitinib-aumolertinib联合方案较化疗显著改善EGFR突变、MET扩增晚期NSCLC患者EGFR-TKI进展后的PFS，安全性可控；这些发现支持双EGFR/MET抑制作为该生物标志物选择人群的新治疗选择。
papers.ai_note: 主要终点PFS阳性，但OS数据未成熟，摘要结论中的“新治疗选择”主要基于PFS获益；开放标签设计可能影响ORR/DoR等非盲态评估的次要终点解读；随访时间较短（11.2个月），长期生存获益尚不明确。

pico.p: 局部晚期或转移性EGFR突变、MET扩增（FISH：平均MET拷贝数≥5或MET/CEP7≥2）且EGFR-TKI进展后NSCLC患者，共314例（dalmelitinib-aumolertinib组156例，铂类化疗组158例）
pico.ic: 干预：dalmelitinib（MET-TKI）联合aumolertinib（第三代EGFR-TKI）；对照：铂类为基础化疗；1:1随机

papers.reason: 为EGFR-TKI耐药后MET扩增晚期NSCLC提供随机III期证据，可能改变该生物标志物人群的后线治疗选择，并支持双EGFR/MET抑制策略的临床定位。
papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: MET amplification accounts for up to 30% of acquired resistance to EGFR-TKI, especially following third-generation EGFR-TKI treatment, yet precision-targeted therapeutic options remain limited. Early-phase studies demonstrated promising antitumor activity with the MET-TKI dalmelitinib combined with the third-generation EGFR-TKI aumolertinib. This phase 3 trial compared dalmelitinib-aumolertinib with platinum-based chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated, MET-amplified advanced NSCLC after EGFR-TKIs progression. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This randomized, open-label, phase 3 trial (NCT06110663) enrolled patients with locally advanced or metastatic EGFR-mutated, MET-amplified NSCLC after EGFR-TKI progression. MET amplification was defined by fluorescence in situ hybridization as a mean MET copy number ≥5 or MET/CEP7 ratio ≥2. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to dalmelitinib-aumolertinib or platinum-based chemotherapy groups. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS) assessed by blinded independent central review per RECIST 1.1. Secondary endpoints included overall survival, objective response rate (ORR), duration of response (DoR), and safety. RESULTS: A total of 314 enrolled patients were assigned to dalmelitinib-aumolertinib (n=156) or platinum-based chemotherapy (n=158). Median follow-up was 11.2 months at the data cutoff date (December 10, 2025). Median PFS was 6.2 months with dalmelitinib-aumolertinib and 4.4 months with chemotherapy (HR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.45 to 0.81; P <0.001). Corresponding ORRs were 59.6% and 38.6%, and median DoRs were 9.7 months and 4.4 months, respectively. Overall survival data were immature. Grade ≥3 treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 50.0% and 51.0% of patients, respectively. Toxicity profiles differed, with more hepatic laboratory abnormalities with dalmelitinib-aumolertinib and more hematologic toxicities with chemotherapy. CONCLUSION: The dalmelitinib-aumolertinib combination significantly improved PFS versus chemotherapy, with a manageable safety profile in advanced EGFR-mutated, MET-amplified NSCLC after progression on EGFR-TKI. These findings support dual EGFR/ MET inhibition as a new treatment option in this biomarker selected population.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer have poor outcomes, with a median overall survival of approximately 12 to 13 months. Tarlatamab (a bispecific T-cell engager targeting delta-like ligand 3 [DLL3] and CD3) was previously shown to improve survival as second-line therapy. Whether adding tarlatamab to durvalumab (an anti-programmed death ligand 1 agent) after initial chemoimmunotherapy could significantly improve survival in the context of maintenance therapy after first remission has been unclear. METHODS: In this phase 3, international, open-label, randomized trial, we compared tarlatamab-durvalumab with durvalumab as first-line maintenance therapy in patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer without progression after initial chemoimmunotherapy. Overall survival and progression-free survival were assessed from randomization at the start of maintenance therapy as the primary and key secondary end points, respectively. Results of the prespecified interim analysis (data-cutoff date, July 7, 2026) are reported here. RESULTS: A total of 563 patients were randomly assigned to receive tarlatamab-durvalumab (282 patients) or durvalumab (281 patients). At a median follow-up of 15.9 months in the tarlatamab-durvalumab group and 16.1 months in the durvalumab group, the estimated median overall survival was 21.1 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 20.8 to could not be estimated) with tarlatamab-durvalumab and 12.7 months (95% CI, 11.2 to 14.8) with durvalumab (hazard ratio for death, 0.42; 95% CI, 0.32 to 0.54; P<0.001). The median progression-free survival was 7.4 months (95% CI, 5.6 to 9.1) with tarlatamab-durvalumab and 1.9 months (95% CI, 1.9 to 2.0) with durvalumab (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.28 to 0.42; P<0.001). Adverse events of grade 3 or higher occurred in 46.8% of the patients who received tarlatamab-durvalumab and in 40.6% of those who received durvalumab alone. Cytokine release syndrome, mainly of grade 1 or 2, was seen in nearly half the patients receiving tarlatamab-durvalumab. CONCLUSIONS: Tarlatamab-durvalumab maintenance therapy resulted in significantly longer overall survival and progression-free survival than durvalumab alone among patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer. (Funded by Amgen and AstraZeneca; DeLLphi-305 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06211036.).

papers.title_en: Sacituzumab Tirumotecan plus Pembrolizumab in PD-L1-Negative Advanced NSCLC.
papers.authors: Zhou F, Meng X, Ding Q, Zhang P, Liang W, Guo S, Yu Y, Yao W et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Oncology, Shanghai East Hospital, Tongji University, Shanghai.
papers.results: BACKGROUND: Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy with a platinum-based agent and pemetrexed is a widely used standard first-line treatment option for patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1)-negative advanced nonsquamo…
papers.reason: 启发式模式收录（未接入语言模型精评）：按期刊层级与研究类型自动入选。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy with a platinum-based agent and pemetrexed is a widely used standard first-line treatment option for patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1)-negative advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without targetable genomic alterations, but outcomes remain suboptimal. METHODS: In this phase 3, open-label, randomized trial, we evaluated sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab in patients with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations and a PD-L1 tumor proportion score of less than 1%. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Overall survival was a secondary end point. This report presents the results of the prespecified interim analysis. RESULTS: A total of 455 patients were randomly assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab (229 patients) or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (226 patients). After a median follow-up of 9.7 months, the median progression-free survival was significantly longer with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab than with chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (15.0 months vs. 5.7 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.49; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.36 to 0.65; P<0.001). An objective response occurred in 50.2% and 47.3% of the patients, respectively, and the median duration of response was 13.6 months and 6.8 months. Overall survival data were immature; the hazard ratio for death was 0.58 (95% CI, 0.38 to 0.88). Adverse events of grade 3 or higher that occurred after the start of treatment were reported in 47.6% of the patients assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab and in 60.6% of those assigned to receive chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. Stomatitis was common with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab, but the events were predominantly grade 1 or 2. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with PD-L1-negative advanced nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations, first-line treatment with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab led to significantly longer progression-free survival than chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. (Funded by Sichuan Kelun-Biotech Biopharmaceutical; OptiTROP-Lung06 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06711900.).

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib is a first-line standard of care for advanced clear-cell renal-cell carcinoma (ccRCC). The phase 3 LITESPARK-012 study (NCT04736706) evaluated efficacy and safety of adding belzutifan (HIF-2α inhibitor) or quavonlimab (anti-CTLA-4) to this regimen. PARTICIPANTS AND METHODS: Adults with previously untreated advanced ccRCC were randomized 1:1:1 to 400 mg pembrolizumab IV Q6W plus 20 mg lenvatinib orally daily and 120 mg belzutifan orally daily (Arm A); coformulated quavonlimab/pembrolizumab 25 mg/400 mg IV Q6W (collectively called MK-1308A) plus lenvatinib (Arm B); or standard-of-care pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib (Control). Treatment continued until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or withdrawal from study; pembrolizumab or quavonlimab/pembrolizumab were administered for a maximum of ∼2 years. Progression-free survival (PFS) by blinded independent central review and overall survival (OS) were dual primary endpoints, tested in all randomized participants for Arm A versus Control, and in participants with IMDC intermediate/poor risk or all participants for Arm B versus Control. Safety was a secondary endpoint. RESULTS: Overall, 560 participants were randomized to Arm A, 562 to Arm B, and 566 to Control. As of the data cutoff date (February 4, 2026), median follow-up was 43.6 months (range, 31.8-57.4). Among all participants, median PFS was 20.8 months in Arm A (HR vs Control: 1.08, 95%CI 0.93-1.26; P=0.8408), 20.7 months in Arm B (HR vs Control: 1.07, 95%CI 0.92-1.25; nominal P=0.8174), and 23.7 months in the Control arm; median OS was 52.0 months in Arm A (HR vs Control: 1.04, 95%CI 0.87-1.25; P=0.6622), not reached (NR) in Arm B (HR vs Control: 1.12, 95%CI 0.94-1.35; nominal P=0.8955), and NR in the Control arm. Among participants with intermediate/poor risk, median PFS was 20.5 months in Arm B and 23.5 months in the Control arm (HR 1.12, 95%CI 0.94-1.33; P=0.8954); median OS was 39.1 versus 46.2 months (HR 1.17, 95%CI 0.96-1.42; P=0.9419). Any-grade all-cause adverse events led to any-drug discontinuation in 51.6%, 51.4%, and 36.2% of participants in the A, B, and Control arms. CONCLUSIONS: Neither addition of the HIF-2α inhibitor belzutifan nor the CTLA-4 inhibitor quavonlimab to pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib improved outcomes in participants with previously untreated advanced RCC versus pembrolizumab and lenvatinib alone. Higher drug discontinuation rates due to adverse events occurred in the investigational arms. Efficacy and safety of standard-of-care pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib was consistent with prior reports.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pembrolizumab, alone or combined with platinum-based chemotherapy, is a standard first-line treatment for patients with metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without actionable oncogenic alterations and with high programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression. We conducted a head-to-head comparison of these two treatment strategies. METHODS: In this multicenter, phase III trial (PERSEE, NCT04547504), adult patients with treatment-naïve stage IV or unresectable stage III NSCLC not amenable to definitive radiotherapy and PD-L1 expression ≥50% were randomly (1:1) assigned to receive pembrolizumab (200 mg every 3 weeks, for up to 35 cycles) or pembrolizumab in combination with four cycles of induction chemotherapy, stratified according to the presence of brain metastases and histologic subtype. Patients with non-squamous histology received cisplatin or carboplatin (AUC 5) plus pemetrexed, followed by pembrolizumab-pemetrexed maintenance; patients with squamous histology received carboplatin (AUC 6) plus paclitaxel, followed by pembrolizumab maintenance. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS), assessed by blinded central review according to RECIST v1.1. Key secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), objective response rate, duration of response, and safety. RESULTS: A total of 321 patients underwent randomization, with 160 assigned to pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy and 161 to pembrolizumab monotherapy. At a median follow-up of 38.7 months, median PFS was significantly longer with combination therapy than with monotherapy (16.1 months [95% CI, 11.0-34.1] vs. 6.9 months [95% CI, 5.5-9.3]; hazard ratio (HR), 0.56; 95% CI, 0.43-0.74; P<0.001). Median OS was 50.2 months versus 29.9 months, respectively (HR, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.56-1.05). Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 54% and 19% of patients, respectively; grade ≥3 immune-related adverse events occurred in 13% of patients in each group. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with treatment-naïve advanced NSCLC and high PD-L1 expression, the addition of platinum-based chemotherapy to pembrolizumab significantly prolonged PFS compared with pembrolizumab monotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Divarasib, a next-generation, oral KRAS G12C inhibitor, is more potent and selective in vitro than the first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib. METHODS: In this phase 3, international, open-label trial, patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were randomly assigned to receive divarasib orally at a dose of 400 mg once daily or control treatment (sotorasib orally at a dose of 960 mg once daily or adagrasib orally at a dose of 600 mg twice daily) until the occurrence of disease progression, unacceptable adverse events, loss of clinical benefit, withdrawal of consent, death, or trial termination. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival, confirmed overall response, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, and safety. RESULTS: A total of 338 patients received divarasib (167 patients) or control treatment (171 patients; 156 received sotorasib and 15 received adagrasib). The median follow-up was 14.3 months. The median progression-free survival was 9.8 months with divarasib and 5.7 months with control treatment (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.44 to 0.76; P<0.001). The median overall survival was 17.7 months with divarasib and 12.0 months with control treatment (hazard ratio for death, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.41 to 0.78; P<0.001). Of the 328 patients who could be evaluated for response, a confirmed response occurred in 58.4% in the divarasib group and in 32.3% in the control group. The median duration of response was 11.9 months with divarasib and 6.9 months with control treatment. Fewer grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were noted with divarasib (24.6%) than with control treatment (34.5%). CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic NSCLC, divarasib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than control treatment. (Supported by F. Hoffmann-La Roche; Krascendo 1 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06497556.).

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is highly lethal owing to its early and aggressive metastasis, yet the underlying multi-layer molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood, limiting therapeutic advances. METHODS: We performed integrative multi-omics profiling (including genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and lactylome) on 99 matched primary tumor, metastatic lymph nodes, and normal esophagus tissue samples from 36 patients with metastatic ESCC. Molecular changes and cross-omics interactions associated with the metastatic cascades were characterized. Key findings were validated by immunohistochemistry and survival analysis in an independent cohort of 116 ESCC patients. Further functional and mechanistic studies were conducted using in vitro and a tail-vein experimental lung metastasis model. RESULTS: Our analysis revealed pronounced disturbance in immune-related pathways closely associated with metastatic progression and poor prognosis. Intercellular adhesion molecule 1 (ICAM1) was identified as a critical factor of ESCC invasion and metastasis. Additionally, lysine-lactylated proteins were predominantly involved in cytoskeleton, focal adhesion and glycolysis pathways during ESCC metastasis. Integrative analysis revealed that the lactylome interacts with the genome and transcriptome through both cis- and trans-regulatory mechanisms, primarily in immune and metabolic pathways. Notably, lactylation of phosphoglycerate mutase 1 (PGAM1) at residue K251 enhances its interaction with actin gamma 1 and promotes metastatic phenotypes. ICAM1 and PGAM1 K251 lactylation represent two independent metastasis-associated mechanisms identified from the same multi-omics dataset. CONCLUSIONS: This integrative multi-omics characterization provides a comprehensive resource for metastatic ESCC research and identifies K251-lactylated PGAM1 as a candidate prognostic biomarker and mechanistic lead warranting further preclinical validation.

papers.abstract_en: Advanced thymic carcinoma is a rare, aggressive malignancy with limited treatment options after chemotherapy failure. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (AL3810-202) aimed to evaluate lucitanib, a novel, orally potent tyrosine kinase inhibitor targeting VEGFR1‒3, FGFR1‒3, and PDGFRα/β in patients with advanced thymic carcinoma progressing after chemotherapy. Sixty-eight patients were randomized (2:1) to receive 10 mg lucitanib daily (n = 46) or placebo (n = 22). Although this study did not meet its primary endpoint of independent review committee (IRC)-assessed progression-free survival (PFS) (median 5.8 vs. 3.7 months; hazard ratio [HR]: 0.60; p = 0.1050), the prespecified log-rank test may have underestimated the treatment effect due to an observed non-proportional hazards pattern. Subsequent restricted mean survival time analysis demonstrated a statistically significant PFS benefit (p < 0.05), which was further supported by significantly prolonged investigator-assessed PFS (6.6 vs. 1.9 months; HR: 0.53; p = 0.0306). The most common grade 3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) were hypertension (50%), proteinuria (15.2%), and thrombocytopenia (8.7%), with no grade 4/5 events. Considering the totality of the evidence and an acceptable safety profile, lucitanib may confer a meaningful clinical benefit for patients with advanced thymic carcinoma, warranting further investigation.

papers.abstract_en: Purpose ENTRÉE Lung (NCT03739710) was a global, open-label, platform study investigating novel immunotherapy combinations in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) following progression on anti-PD-(L)1 and platinum-based treatment. We report findings with dostarlimab (anti-PD-1) plus belrestotug (anti-TIGIT) with or without nelistotug (anti-CD96). Patients and Methods The study included safety cohorts with dose escalation and expansion: Arm 4 safety cohort (Arm4-safety), dostarlimab 500 mg plus belrestotug 200-1000 mg (initial dose level: 400 mg); Arm5-safety, dostarlimab 500 mg plus belrestotug 400 mg and nelistotug 210-1400 mg (initial dose level: 700 mg); study treatments were administered intravenously every 3 weeks. A randomized cohort was added to Arm 5 (Arm5-randomized), assigning patients to nelistotug 210 or 1400 mg in the triplet combination. Primary endpoints were safety and tolerability. Results Sixty-two patients were enrolled (n=24 Arm4-safety; n=17 Arm5-safety; n=21 Arm5-randomized [n=11, 200 mg; n=10, 1400 mg]). Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 4 (17%), 1 (6%) and 3 (14%) patients in Arm4-safety, Arm5-safety and Arm5-randomized, respectively. There were few treatment discontinuations due to adverse events. Most patients exhibited progressive disease as best response. There was one partial response (Arm5-randomized, 210 mg); stable disease ≥12 weeks was experienced by 4 (17%), 5 (29%) and 2 (10%) patients in Arm4-safety, Arm5-safety and Arm5-randomized, respectively. Conclusions Dostarlimab plus belrestotug, with or without nelistotug, was well tolerated but demonstrated no clinically meaningful activity in previously treated advanced NSCLC. Further research is required to identify patients who may benefit from other immunotherapy combinations.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Anastomotic leakage after oesophagectomy is common, and associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence angiography has emerged as a promising intraoperative adjunct for perfusion assessment at the anastomotic site. This study aims to assess the impact of ICG use on anastomotic leakage rates and postoperative outcomes. METHODS: A PRISMA-compliant systematic search of Medline, PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library was performed. The primary outcome was anastomotic leakage. Key secondary outcomes were conduit necrosis, mortality, and reoperation; all secondary outcomes were reported. The Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies - of Interventions (ROBINS-I) and Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tools were used for investigating risk of bias. Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) was used to assess certainty of evidence. A random-effects meta-analysis and meta-regression as well as subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed. RESULTS: From 902 identified studies, 23 met the inclusion criteria (including 4 RCTs; 2845 patients, of whom 1154 underwent ICG assessment). ICG use was associated with reduced anastomotic leakage rates (OR 0.44 (95% c.i. 0.29 to 0.65), P < 0.001; number needed to treat = 13) and conduit necrosis rates (OR 0.32 (95% c.i. 0.12 to 0.85), P = 0.022). Mortality (OR 1.43 (95% c.i. 0.69 to 2.97), P = 0.335), reoperation (OR 0.84 (95% c.i. 0.51 to 1.39), P = 0.500), severe anastomotic leakage, overall morbidity, readmission, operating time, and length of stay did not differ between groups. Certainty of evidence was low or very low across all outcomes (GRADE), predominantly driven by the observational study design of many of the studies. CONCLUSION: Use of ICG appears to be associated with reduced anastomotic leak in oesophagectomy, although certainty of evidence is low. Assessment remains qualitative and operator-dependent.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Risk stratification before esophageal and gastric endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) in older adults often relies on age and comorbidity; however, these measures may not capture vulnerability reflected in routinely collected claims data. We aimed to evaluate the claims-based frailty and short-term adverse events association after esophageal and gastric endoscopic submucosal dissection. METHODS: We used a nationwide Japanese administrative database to identify patients aged ≥ 75 years who underwent first esophageal or gastric ESD. Frailty was defined using the Hospital Frailty Risk Score (HFRS), calculated from diagnoses during a 2 year lookback period. After 1:1 propensity score matching, frail and non-frail patients were compared. The primary outcome was binary composite of short-term adverse events, including in-hospital perforation/peritonitis, delayed bleeding, thromboembolism, aspiration pneumonia, and 30 day all-cause mortality. Component outcomes, survival, length of stay, costs, and readmission were also evaluated. RESULTS: Among 15,184 eligible patients, 4,970 matched pairs were included. Frailty was associated with the composite adverse outcome (adjusted odds ratio 1.35; 95% confidence interval 1.19-1.53), driven mainly by perforation/peritonitis and delayed bleeding. No significant differences were observed for 30 day mortality, thromboembolic events, or aspiration pneumonia. Frailty was also associated with lower overall survival during follow-up, whereas median length of stay was identical between groups. CONCLUSION: Among older adults undergoing esophageal or gastric ESD, HFRS-defined claims-based frailty was associated with higher rates of short-term adverse events, particularly perforation/peritonitis and delayed bleeding. These findings suggest that routinely collected claims data may help identify vulnerable patients who warrant closer peri-procedural assessment and monitoring.

papers.abstract_en: Trimerization motifs play pivotal roles in structural biology and therapeutic protein engineering. Here, we describe a short trimerization motif (rFd1303) derived from the Reoviridae family reovirus σ1 protein. Compared with the widely used T4-Foldon, the rFd1303 increased recombinant protein yields. The rFd1303-fused immunogens of SARS-CoV-2 spike and influenza hemagglutinin elicited antibody responses comparable to T4-Foldon-fused controls in mice. Using this tag, we engineered a trimeric ACE2-Ig fusion protein (TriACE2-Ig) that remained stable after 30 days at room temperature and neutralized a broad range of ACE2-utilizing sarbecoviruses, including 19 SARS-CoV-2 variants, SARS-CoV, and pangolin coronaviruses GD and GX, with higher potency than monomeric ACE2-Ig. In the hamster model challenged with various SARS-CoV-2 variants, our data demonstrated that intranasal TriACE2-Ig administration markedly reduced viral loads, virus-induced body-weight loss, lung pathology, and decreased within-cage virus transmission. These findings highlight rFd1303 as a versatile trimerization platform for vaccine and therapeutic protein development.

papers.abstract_en: VEGF-A/VEGF-R axis is well recognized for its role in tumor angiogenesis as well as tumor-induced immunosuppressive mechanisms. Targeting this pathway can help to switch tumor microenvironment toward a more immune-permissive state. Inhibition of VEGF-A/VEGFR has emerged as a strategy to enhance the efficacy of immunotherapy in some cancers leading to the approval of anti-VEGF-A/anti-PD(L)1 combinations in advanced renal cell cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, non-small cell lung cancer, and endometrial cancer. However, in other tumor types, and particularly in colorectal cancer or glioblastoma, results remain limited. In this review, we discuss the biological rationale underlying anti-VEGF-A/PD-(L)1 combinations, summarize the clinical evidence supporting their use across tumor types, discuss the disappointing results in colorectal cancer and glioblastoma, and highlight emerging strategies to improve their therapeutic efficacy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive fibrotic interstitial lung disease with high morbidity and mortality. Inhaled treprostinil showed pulmonary vascular and lung-function signals in pulmonary hypertension associated with Interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD) and was subsequently tested in IPF trials. OBJECTIVES: This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the efficacy and safety of inhaled treprostinil in adults with IPF. METHODS: PubMed, Google Scholar and the Cochrane Library/CENTRAL were searched for records published from January 2000 to 2026. A random-effects meta-analysis used the DerSimonian-Laird tau squared and inverse-variance weighting methods. Continuous outcomes were pooled as generic inverse-variance effects from reported estimates and 95% confidence intervals. Hazard ratios were pooled on the log scale. Safety outcomes were pooled as risk ratios from event counts. RESULTS: The searches identified 1552 records. After deduplication, 379 records were screened and 85 full-text reports were assessed. Eleven reports were included in the systematic review. TETON-1 and TETON-2 were the two direct-IPF randomized trials within the coordinated TETON program eligible for primary meta-analysis. Inhaled treprostinil improved absolute forced vital capacity (FVC) change at 52 weeks compared with placebo (MD 111.28 mL, 95% CI 77.61 to 144.95, p < 0.001; I squared 8.5%). Clinical worsening was reduced (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.57 to 0.84, p < 0.001; I squared 0.0%). Acute exacerbation was lower in pooled analysis (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.30 to 0.91, p = 0.022), while all-cause mortality did not differ significantly (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.47 to 1.05, p = 0.086). Adverse-event discontinuation, cough and headache were more frequent with treprostinil. CONCLUSIONS: In direct IPF randomized evidence, inhaled treprostinil preserved lung function and reduced clinical worsening at 52 weeks.

papers.abstract_en: Population-based lung cancer screening with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) is expanding across Europe, including a publicly funded Polish programme starting in October 2026. Because screening-eligible individuals share substantial tobacco-related cardiovascular risk, LDCT also offers cardiovascular risk assessment without additional radiation. We conducted a narrative review of the PubMed literature published up to September 2026, prioritising guidelines, lung cancer screening cohorts and systematic reviews. We summarise the cardiovascular findings on non-contrast, non-electrocardiography (ECG)-gated LDCT: coronary artery, aortic valve, mitral annular and thoracic aortic calcification, ascending aortic dilatation, pericardial effusion, and pulmonary artery enlargement, as well as investigational cardiac volumetry, epicardial adipose tissue and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted quantification. We grade each finding by reportability, defined downstream action and supporting evidence, and align reporting thresholds with the European Respiratory Society/European Society of Thoracic Imaging (ERS/ESTI) statement on incidental findings. LDCT cannot replace dedicated cardiac imaging or establish haemodynamic diagnoses. The prognostic value of coronary and aortic valve calcification and of ascending aortic dilatation is established, whereas the evidence for mitral annular calcification and pulmonary artery enlargement is more limited; observational data indicate that reporting these markers changes preventive management, but whether this improves cardiovascular outcomes has not yet been demonstrated. Standardised reporting, proportionate thresholds, and coordinated pathways linking radiology, pulmonology, primary care and cardiology are needed to translate incidental cardiovascular findings into scalable prevention and should be evaluated in implementation studies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The marked heterogeneity of primary liver cancer (PLC), together with the dynamic influence of the tumor microenvironment (TME), remains a major challenge to precision oncology. As currently available therapies provide limited benefit for many patients and robust preclinical platforms for rapid, patient-specific treatment stratification are lacking, there is an urgent need for models that faithfully preserve individual tumor architecture and cellular diversity. METHODS: We established three-dimensional bioprinted primary liver cancer (3DP-PLC) models comprising 61 patient-derived monocultures and 34 co-culture models with patient-matched cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs). To explore the correlation between ex vivo models and clinical drug response, we developed a clinically anchored hybrid stratification framework for response classification. In parallel, the 3DP-PLC/CAF co-culture biobank was used to investigate stromal regulation of therapeutic response. RESULTS: These 3DP-PLC constructs preserved the histological features, biomarker expression patterns, mutational landscapes, and transcriptomic profiles of their corresponding parental tumors. Drug-sensitivity profiling across the biobank revealed substantial intertumoral heterogeneity in therapeutic responses. The clinically anchored hybrid stratification framework integrating ex vivo pharmaceutical profiles with external clinical benchmark data enabled interpretable response classification and demonstrated clinical relevance in patients receiving neoadjuvant or adjuvant targeted therapy. In parallel, the 3DP-PLC/CAF co-culture biobank, combined with single-cell transcriptomic analysis, recapitulated fibrous ring-like architecture and revealed CAF-associated drug-resistant states. CONCLUSIONS: These findings support 3DP-PLC as a high-fidelity and scalable platform for personalized therapeutic stratification and mechanistic investigation of tumor-stroma interactions in PLC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Global antibiotic use during the COVID-19 pandemic and its impact remain unclear. This study analysed antibiotic use, bacterial co-infections, and the association between antibiotic use and in-hospital mortality among patients hospitalised for COVID-19, using a WHO database. METHODS: We conducted a multicountry cohort study using anonymised patient-level data from The WHO Global Clinical Platform for COVID-19. Data were collected across 64 countries in all six WHO regions between January, 2020, and October, 2023. The study included hospitalised patients of all ages with suspected or confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. We obtained patient-level data from standardised WHO case report forms completed prospectively or retrospectively and from harmonised national registries, research studies, and hospital databases. Patients without a suspected or confirmed COVID-19 diagnosis or missing information on hospital admission date, antibiotic use, or outcome were excluded from the analysis. Patients were followed up from hospital admission until death, discharge, transfer, or 28 days, whichever occurred first. Follow-up data were collected at hospital discharge or death by the treating facility and entered into the platform. The primary outcome was 28-day in-hospital mortality, and we analysed this outcome using Cox proportional hazards models with a shared frailty term to account for country-level clustering. FINDINGS: The median age of the study population was 61·9 years (±21·7), with 198 223 women and 251 990 men with data available on antibiotic use. Of the 592 898 patients enrolled, 451 291 (76·1%) had data on antibiotic use and were included in the descriptive analysis; 122 854 had complete data on empirical treatment type, of whom 47 359 (38·5%) were included in the regression analysis. Among the 451 291 patients with data on antibiotic use, 341 125 (75·6%) received antibiotics, more frequently in severe to critical cases than in mild to moderate cases (80·5% vs 71·6%). Prescribing was highest in the Eastern Mediterranean (83·0%) and African (82·7%) regions and lowest in the Western Pacific region (32·8%), declining in the European region and region of the Americas but increasing in the African region between 2020 and 2022. Treatment was predominantly empirical and involved Watch antibiotics of the WHO Access, Watch, and Reserve classification. Clinically suspected co-infections were reported in 47 050 (7·9%) of the 592 898 patients; among those with positive cultures, 1815 (42·8%) of 4237 had multidrug-resistant bacteria. In the unadjusted analyses, empirical antibiotic use was associated with higher mortality across severity strata. After adjustment for age, sex, comorbidities, and disease severity, empirical antibiotic use remained associated with increased mortality in mild to moderate cases (adjusted hazard ratio 1·80, 95% CI 1·36-2·38) and severe to critical cases (1·16, 1·08-1·24). INTERPRETATION: Despite clinically suspected co-infections being reported in only 47 050 (7·9%) of the 592 898 enrolled patients, 341 125 (75·6%) of the 451 291 patients with data on antibiotic use received antibiotic therapy, predominantly broad-spectrum agents. As antibiotic use was not associated with improved clinical outcomes and is known to increase antimicrobial resistance, it should be rationalised through strengthened antimicrobial stewardship and behavioural interventions, particularly during respiratory viral epidemics. papers.abstract_en: Patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remain at high risk of relapse despite perioperative treatment1-3. NeoCOAST-2 (NCT05061550), a phase 2, randomised platform trial, tested novel perioperative treatments in patients with stage IIA-IIIB NSCLC. At primary analysis, combining standard chemotherapy plus durvalumab (anti-PD-L1 antibody) with oleclumab (Arm 1, n = 76), monalizumab (Arm 2, n = 72) or datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd; Arm 4, n = 54) resulted in pathological complete response (pCR) rates of 20.3%, 25.7%, and 35.2%, respectively4. Here, we present the first report of prespecified secondary endpoints of event-free survival (EFS) and circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) clearance, and exploratory analyses of associations between ctDNA dynamics and clinical outcomes. The 24-month EFS rates were 70.5%, 75.7% and 77.9% in Arms 1, 2 and 4, respectively. Using a tumour-agnostic assay, ctDNA clearance at neoadjuvant Cycle 3 Day 1 was highest in Arm 4 (50.9%, 54.5%, and 72.5% in each arm, respectively). ctDNA clearance correlated with prolonged EFS versus non-clearance (pooled hazard ratio (HR) 0.22; 95% CI = 0.11-0.45, P = 0.0000443). Patients with both ctDNA clearance and pCR had favourable EFS outcomes versus those with neither (EFS HR 0.10, 95% CI = 0.02-0.42, P = 0.002). These findings suggest combined assessment of ctDNA clearance and pCR may improve risk stratification, and that the numerically highest pCR4 and EFS rates with the Dato-DXd combination warrant further evaluation.

papers.abstract_en: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) lacks effective targeted therapies, and how metabolic reprogramming drives oncogenic signaling remains poorly defined. Here, we identify histone H3 lysine 23 lactylation (H3K23la) as a key epigenetic mediator linking lactate accumulation to tumor progression. H3K23la is upregulated in ESCC and correlates with poor prognosis. Mechanistically, H3K23la promotes WNK lysine deficient protein kinase 1 (WNK1) transcription, which increases histone H3 Ser10 phosphorylation (p-H3S10) and enhances AKT transcription, thereby driving PI3K-AKT signaling. This defines a lactate-H3K23la-WNK1-p-H3S10-AKT axis connecting metabolism to oncogenic signaling. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of WNK1 by CD03017 disrupts this pathway and suppresses tumor growth in vitro and in patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models. In conclusion, our findings define a metabolic-epigenetic-signaling axis in ESCC and establish WNK1 as a potential therapeutic target downstream of histone lactylation.

papers.abstract_en: Previous studies have demonstrated promising results for radiolabeled fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET/CT in gastric cancer (GC) when compared with [18F]FDG PET/CT. In this prospective clinical trial, we assessed the impact of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT compared with [18F]FDG PET/CT and contrast-enhanced CT (ceCT) on primary staging and management of Danish patients with GC and gastroesophageal junction cancer (GEJC). Methods: Between February 8, 2024, and September 26, 2025, consecutive patients with GC or GEJC who were candidates for surgical resection and perioperative chemotherapy were included in this trial. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT images were deidentified and presented to the treating clinicians after the trial, at which point [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT-based staging and tentative patient management were determined. Results: Twenty patients were included in the trial, including 15 (75%) with GEJC and 5 (25%) with GC; all patients were diagnosed with adenocarcinoma. For the primary tumor, [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 and [18F]FDG PET/CT agreed in 18 (90%) of cases, and both modalities demonstrated a detection rate of 90% (95% CI, 68%-99%). For clinical nodal staging, ceCT detected more lymph nodes than did [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET and [18F]FDG PET alone (81 vs. 53 vs. 44, respectively). [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET did not detect additional lymph nodes beyond those detected with ceCT. Despite detecting fewer lymph nodes overall, [18F]FDG PET identified 6 additional lymph nodes in 5 patients, resulting in clinical nodal upstaging in 4 cases (20%) compared with both [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET and ceCT. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET would have led to clinical metastatic upstaging in 4 patients (20%) because of the identification of potential distant metastases (1 peritoneal and 3 liver metastases), which would have resulted in a change in recommended patient management from curative-intent to palliative treatment in 3 patients (15%). Conclusion: The primary clinical value of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET was its ability to detect distant metastases that were negative on [18F]FDG PET and ceCT, potentially impacting patient management. There were no obvious advantages in the evaluation of primary tumor and regional lymph nodes. Although the study population is relatively small and mostly consists of patients with GEJC, this study represents the first prospective investigation of consecutive patients in a well-defined, clinical northern European setting and indicates potential future roles for [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET in GC and GEJC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic was a prolonged period of traumatic stress with potentially lasting health impacts, especially for vulnerable groups including pregnant individuals. Prenatal stress has been associated with greater risk of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDD), warranting investigation of prenatal pandemic-related traumatic stress (PTS) as a risk factor for NDD. METHODS: We surveyed Kaiser Permanente Northern California (KPNC) members who were ≥ 12 weeks pregnant between June 2020 and September 2022. PTS was measured using the 10-item PTS Scale and modeled as a continuous total symptom score (range: 0-10) and binary exposure (high, ≥ 9; low, < 9). We prospectively followed children through July 2025 and linked to sociodemographic and medical characteristics, including NDD diagnoses, in KPNC electronic records. We fit Cox regression models adjusted for maternal age, race and ethnicity, insurance type, SARS-CoV-2 infection, pre-pregnancy BMI, pre-pregnancy depression, child birthyear and sex to estimate hazard ratios (HR) for any NDD and separately for autism spectrum disorder (ASD) associated with PTS and evaluated effect modification by child sex. RESULTS: Of 13,859 mothers, 21.1% identified as Asian, 3.0% as Black, 19.6% as Hispanic, 4.6% as Multiracial, < 1.0% as Native American or Pacific Islander, 49.0% as White, and 1.7% were of Unknown race. The mean (SD) PTS score was 3.9 (2.6) and 722 (5.2%) mothers had high PTS (≥ 9); 2,750 (19.8%) children were diagnosed with any NDD and 651 (4.7%) with ASD. Higher PTS symptom score was associated with significantly greater risk of any NDD (HR = 1.02, 95% CI = 1.01-1.04) and ASD (HR = 1.04 [1.01-1.07]) per 1-point increase in continuous score. High compared to low PTS was associated with greater risk of NDD diagnoses (HR = 1.18 [1.01-1.37]) and ASD (HR = 1.20 [0.89-1.62]), although not statistically significant for ASD. Associations did not differ by sex for NDD (HRFemales= 1.20 [0.92-1.56], HRMales= 1.17 [0.96-1.41]; interaction P = 0.78) or ASD (HRFemales= 1.31 [0.73-2.34], HRMales= 1.17 [0.82-1.65]; interaction P = 0.60). CONCLUSIONS: Among this cohort of mothers who were pregnant during the COVID-19 pandemic, higher PTS was associated with greater risk of child NDD diagnoses. Further research is needed to investigate the potential biologic mechanisms underlying this association.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Bipolar disorder (BD) manifests both genetic predispositions and brain imaging abnormalities. Genetic analyses provide a powerful approach to disentangling the associations between BD and brain imaging-derived phenotype (IDP). However, in East Asian (EAS) populations, the genetic basis of these neuroimaging changes and their clinical relevance remains underexplored due to limited integrative evidence. METHODS: We investigated the genetic architecture and clinical relevance of BD and brain IDPs in East Asian populations using individual-level data from the Chinese Bipolar Disorder (CN-BD) cohort (N = 3,920), summary statistics of BD from the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium (PGC) (N = 16,915) and of IDPs from the CHIMGEN Consortium (N = 7,058), and genotype and clinical data from the Chinese Longitudinal and Systematic Study of Bipolar Disorder cohort (CLASS-BD). We employed genetic correlation (GNOVA), multi-trait meta-analysis (MTAG, CPASSOC), and ancestry-specific fine-mapping (MESuSiE) to identify shared genetic loci. Functional annotation, protein association (SMR, BLISS), and spatiotemporal expression trajectory analyses were conducted. Bidirectional Mendelian Randomization (MR) assessed causal relationships, and polygenic risk score (PRS)-PheWAS explored phenome-level associations with clinical traits. RESULTS: Our multi-trait meta-analysis identified 11 pleiotropic single nucleotide variants (SNVs) implicated in BD-IDP pairs, showing convergent enrichment in lipid metabolism and neurotransmitter biosynthesis pathways. Fine-mapping revealed an EAS-specific causal signal (rs7941324 near RPS27P20), which demonstrated high posterior inclusion probability in EAS but not European ancestries, and colocalized with BD and specific brain alterations. MR revealed 27 IDP-to-BD and 35 BD-to-IDP causal relationships, distinguishing structural changes of the parietal and temporal gyri as markers preceding BD onset and the right precuneus area as a state marker that followed BD onset. Clinically, BD-IDP polygenic risk scores were significantly associated with depressive symptoms, anxiety, and suicide risk. Mediation analysis further indicated that depressive and anxiety symptoms statistically mediated the relationship between BD-IDP PRS and suicide risk. Moreover, PRS-PheWAS identified 135 significant associations with metabolic phenotypes, highlighting a psycho-metabolic nexus in BD. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings reveal associations between polygenicity and distinct BD brain patterns and clinical profiles. We identified ancestry-specific causal variants and bidirectional BD-IDP relationships. PRS associations with depressive symptoms, anxiety, suicide risk, and metabolic phenotypes highlight precision medicine potential for BD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI) after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) is increasingly attributed to thromboinflammation and microvascular platelet activation. Accordingly, we aimed to characterize longitudinal platelet aggregation, platelet activation, and platelet morphology in patients with aSAH and assessed their association with DCI. METHODS: This single-center prospective cohort consisted of 206 patients with aSAH. Of the 206 patients, 144 were analyzed via platelet aggregometry, 148 via flow cytometry, and 129 had both aggregometry and flow cytometry data. An additional 52 patients had morphology data. Peripheral blood was sampled on post-bleed days 1, 2, 4, 7, and 10. Platelet aggregation was measured by Chrono-Log aggregometry; platelet activation (PAC-1, CD62P) was measured by flow cytometry; platelet morphology was measured by microscopy. Patient-level area-under-the-curve summaries were entered into binary logistic regression. Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery rate (FDR) was applied across the analyte × parameter grid. RESULTS: Sixty patients (29.1%) developed DCI. Across days 1-10, no agonist-stimulated aggregation parameter and no flow cytometric activation parameter was significantly associated with DCI after FDR correction (all q ≥ 0.42). Only morphologically activated platelets were more prevalent in DCI patients at day 2 (73.8 ± 4.9% vs. 55.6 ± 18.6%; p = 0.001), a difference that survived FDR correction (q = 0.005). CONCLUSIONS: Peripheral platelet function assays do not reliably stratify DCI risk after aSAH. These findings may align with the preferential consumption of the hyperactive platelets, though these findings are hypothesis-generating only and need further investigation.

papers.abstract_en: Tendon healing is the primary goal of tendinopathy therapy. However, the therapeutic response of adjacent muscles remains uninvestigated. MR-elastography (MRE) can assess muscle biomechanical properties and function. This study investigated muscle biomechanical responses in patients treated for patellar (PT) or Achilles tendinopathy (AT). A prospective longitudinal study included 20 athletes, 8 with AT (41 years ± 8; 6 men) and 12 with PT (34 years ± 10; 12 men), who underwent MRI, diffusion-tensor-imaging (DTI), and MRE before and ≥6 months post-treatment. Isotropic (ciso) and anisotropic stiffness parameters (c‖ and c⊥) in tendon-adjacent muscles were derived and analyzed between groups and longitudinally compared with clinical scores and tendon dimensions. At baseline, symptomatic legs with higher tendon dimensions and clinical symptoms exhibited lower muscle stiffness than asymptomatic legs (p<0.05). Post-treatment, AT patients showed increased ciso (4.3±8.5%) in gastrocnemius and posterior soleus (SolP; 4.9±8.6%) in treated legs but decreased SolP stiffness (-3.2±7.2%) in untreated legs (p<0.05). In PT patients, only anisotropic MRE (c‖: 5.3±15.2% and c⊥: 10.3±12.7%) in vastus lateralis showed significant increases (p<0.05) post-treatment. In treated legs of AT and PT, increased muscle stiffness post-treatment correlated negatively with tendon dimensions (p<0.05). Post-therapy, tendon-adjacent muscles exhibited increased stiffness in affected leg and decreased stiffness in contralateral leg (particularly SolP), potentially reflecting altered muscle use and loading, respectively. The observed changes in muscle stiffness may help characterize muscle biomechanical changes during rehabilitation and balanced recovery. Furthermore, anisotropic muscle stiffness was more sensitive to tendon structural changes than isotropic stiffness, warranting further validation for clinical assessment.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Women who use drugs (WWUD) often experience social and economic marginalization. Many rely on survival economies that span formal, informal, and illicit income-generating activities, which may increase exposure to the criminal legal system. This study identified exploratory patterns of survival economic strategies among WWUD, then examined associations between income activities and criminal legal exposures during Baltimore, Maryland's COVID-19 emergency period and de facto drug decriminalization. METHODS: Data come from the baseline assessment a WWUD cohort (n = 227) in Baltimore, recruited from August 2021 to December 2022. Guided by a sociological framework of income sources among low-income women, latent class analysis was used to identify survival economics across state support, instrumental support (money from family, friends, partners), informal labor, and illicit work (selling drugs, sex work). We then assessed associations between two common income sources (illicit and state support) and criminal legal exposures using Poisson regression with robust variance. RESULTS: Three distinct survival economic strategies emerged: mixed and diverse income (57% of sample), primarily state supported (27%), and primarily illicit (15%). Arrest prevalence did not differ across income activities. However, WWUD reporting illicit income compared to not were significantly more likely to report police encounters (adjusted prevalence ratios (aPR) 1.61 95% CI 1.39, 2.01), including abusive ones, although borderline significant (aPR 1.33 95% CI 1.02,1.74). CONCLUSIONS: WWUD engaged in diverse survival economic strategies and illicit income generation was associated with police contact. Although these findings are exploratory, they highlight the importance of clarifying how criminalized survival economies are policed.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Chronic raw opium use can result in opioid use disorder (OUD). Although voxel-based morphometry (VBM) studies have demonstrated decreased gray matter volume (GMV) in heroin-induced OUD, the structural impacts of long-term raw opium consumption remain poorly understood. This study investigated GMV alterations in men with opium-induced OUD and their association with use duration. METHODS: High-resolution T1-weighted MRI scans were acquired from 28 men with opium-induced OUD (mean use duration 17.89 ± 5.85 years) receiving opium tincture maintenance and 25 age- and education-matched healthy male controls. Whole-brain VBM (CAT12/SPM12) was controlled for age, total intracranial volume, and nicotine use. Analysis used a voxel-level uncorrected threshold of p < 0.05 with cluster-level FDR correction (p < 0.05), along with stricter thresholds (uncorrected p < 0.001, TFCE with FWE), and small-volume correction (SVC). Partial correlation and multiple linear regression investigated clinical associations. RESULTS: Whole-brain analysis identified a left-hemisphere cluster of reduced GMV (cluster-level FDR-corrected p = 0.009). No clusters survived p < 0.001 or TFCE with FWE correction. Reductions in the left insula, inferior frontal gyrus, and parahippocampal gyrus remained significant after SVC. Left insula GMV was negatively associated with duration of opium use (partial r = -0.45, p = 0.027; β = -0.48, p = 0.027 in regression). CONCLUSION: Prolonged raw opium use is associated with decreased GMV in areas involved in craving and impulse control. Given that the whole-brain findings were not confirmed by more stringent statistical approaches, the results should be considered exploratory and necessitate replication in larger samples.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCV) reduce invasive disease and routine pediatric infections, yet subtherapeutic antibody responses have been reported in children with refractory otolaryngologic disease. This study evaluated pneumococcal antibody responses in a community cohort of vaccinated children and compared findings with prior specialty cohorts and prelicensure trial data. METHODS: Serum from children aged 15-36 months with a documented four-dose PCV series was analysed for IgG concentrations to 14 serotypes. Protective thresholds were defined for invasive disease (≥0.35 μg/ml) and noninvasive disease (≥1.3 and ≥ 2.0 μg/ml). Results were compared with published pediatric cohorts and prelicensure trial data. RESULTS: Overall, 77.1% of children met the invasive disease threshold. Only 31.3% and 18.8% met the ≥1.3 and ≥ 2.0 μg/ml thresholds, respectively. Antibody levels were consistently lower than those reported in prior cohorts and prelicensure trials across most serotypes. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that real-world immunogenicity following routine PCV may differ from that observed in strictly defined and controlled clinical trial populations, particularly at higher antibody thresholds associated with noninvasive disease. Larger-scale, prospective studies are needed to determine if trends hold across broader cohorts.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Small for gestational age (SGA) infants face neurodevelopmental risks, yet early catch-up growth’s link to later outcomes remains unclear. This study explored associations between catch-up growth (weight, length, head circumference) and neurodevelopment in full-term SGA infants during the first 2 years and developed a prediction model. METHODS: This prospective cohort study enrolled full-term SGA and appropriate for gestational age (AGA) infants from a single centre, yielding 91 SGA and 115 AGA after exclusion. All were followed to 24 months with regular anthropometry. Catch-up was defined as ΔZ ≥0.67 from birth to each time point. Neurodevelopment was assessed by Gesell Developmental Schedules at 24 months. Multivariate linear regression with false discovery rate (FDR) correction and logistic regression for prediction modelling were performed. RESULTS: Catch-up peaked at 8 months (85.71%). After FDR correction, head circumference catch-up showed nominally significant associations with adaptive development at 6 months (β=6.56, p=0.019), 8 months (β=6.89, p=0.013) and 12 months (β=5.63, p=0.045); none survived FDR. Weight and length catch-up showed none. A logistic model with 6-month head circumference catch-up, sex and maternal body mass index showed acceptable calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow p=0.344) and modest discrimination (area under the curve=0.685, 95% CI 0.567 to 0.803). CONCLUSION: Head circumference catch-up showed nominally significant associations with adaptive development—the core Gesell domain—whereas weight/length did not. Achieving head circumference catch-up by 6 months may predict adaptive outcomes at 24 months. Given the exploratory nature, confirmation in independent cohorts is needed before causal inferences can be made.

papers.abstract_en: Birt-Hogg-Dubé (BHD) syndrome is an autosomal dominant tumour predisposition disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the folliculin (FLCN) gene. It is characterized by benign skin tumours, renal neoplasia and cystic lung disease, with a risk of spontaneous pneumothorax. Although historically considered rare, population genomic data indicate that FLCN pathogenic variants are substantially more common than expected from clinically ascertained cases, suggesting that many variant carriers are not currently recognized in clinical practice. Advances in the molecular biology of BHD syndrome have established that FLCN loss-of-function is associated with dysregulation of the mTORC1-TFEB lysosomal signalling pathway, which has been implicated in mouse models of BHD syndrome-associated renal and lung pathology. Clinically, diagnosis relies on recognizing characteristic patterns across dermatological, renal and pulmonary presentations, with genetic confirmation enabling cascade testing and targeted surveillance. Management is centred on lifelong renal imaging, early intervention for tumours, and prevention and treatment of pneumothorax, delivered through multidisciplinary care. Despite generally indolent renal tumour behaviour, malignant progression can occur. Ongoing research aims to improve early diagnosis through population genomics and to develop targeted therapies. These advances are likely to transform the identification and management of BHD syndrome and provide broader insights into tumour suppressor biology.

papers.abstract_en: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from mesenchymal stem or stromal cells (MSCs) have shown therapeutic potential for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), yet reproducible and scalable methods to enhance EV yield and therapeutic potency remain limited. Here, we describe a biophysical priming strategy using pulsed focused ultrasound (pFUS) to apply controlled mechanical stimulation to umbilical cord (UC)-derived MSCs. A single, 1-min exposure generated primed EVs (pUC-EVs) with a 1.9-fold increase in concentration and a therapeutically enhanced molecular cargo, without changes in vesicle size distribution. We demonstrate that this process is mechanistically dependent on calcium influx, as calcium chelation with EGTA markedly reduced pFUS‑induced enhancement of EV secretion. Transcriptomic profiling of UC-MSCs indicated that pFUS activates calcium-dependent mechanotransduction pathways associated with endosomal sorting complexes required for transport (ESCRT) machinery, leading to coordinated upregulation of ESCRT components, vesicle trafficking regulators, while proteomics analysis of UC-EVs revealed enrichment of mitochondrial proteins that support oxidative phosphorylation and ATP generation. Functionally, pUC-EVs exhibit enhanced uptake by macrophages and alveolar epithelial cells, where they increase ATP levels, improve mitochondrial respiration, and promote a reparative, anti-inflammatory macrophage phenotype in vitro. In a lipopolysaccharide-induced juvenile ARDS model, intratracheal delivery of pUC-EVs localized treatment to the injured lung and significantly improved epithelial-endothelial barrier integrity, as shown by reduced vascular leakage, bronchoalveolar lavage protein content, inflammatory mediators, and neutrophil infiltration, alongside improved histological preservation compared with unprimed UC-EVs. A comprehensive in vivo safety assessment demonstrated that pUC-EVs exhibited significantly reduced serum IgG binding compared to UC-EVs, maintained normal coagulation parameter, and preserved organ function (liver, kidney, spleen) with no adverse histopathological changes, supporting a favorable biocompatibility profile. Together, these findings identify mechanopriming by pFUS as a mechanistically defined, well‑tolerated, and scalable approach to enhance EV biogenesis and therapeutic function, supporting the potential application of EVs as a therapy for ARDS and related inflammatory lung diseases.

papers.abstract_en: Understanding charge carrier recombination kinetics is vital for optimizing perovskite materials and devices. Time-resolved photoluminescence (TrPL) is widely used to investigate carrier kinetics, but kinetic parameters inferred from TrPL alone often suffer from intrinsic non-uniqueness. Therefore, quantitatively resolving complex multichannel recombination processes remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the non-uniqueness problem in TrPL. Through incorporating TrPL with excitation-dependent photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY), the non-uniqueness problem is substantially alleviated. Based on this insight, we develop a deep learning (DL) framework to extract kinetic parameters from joint TrPL-PLQY profiles. This framework avoids repeated iterative parameter optimization for each new dataset within the predefined kinetic model. The DL model is trained on a large dataset generated from physically grounded simulations. Six physically relevant key kinetic parameters spanning several orders of magnitude, namely, effective external band-to-band electron-hole bimolecular recombination coefficient (γeh), electron capture coefficient (γec), hole capture coefficient (γhc), trap density (NT), electron emission coefficient (γee), and Auger recombination coefficient (γAug), can be rapidly predicted. High accuracy is achieved, with coefficients of determination of 0.996, 0.938, 0.969, 0.988, 0.905, and 0.973 for the respective parameters. The framework is further validated experimentally. The DL-predicted kinetic parameters are physically consistent with device-level characterization results. Moreover, when working with PLQY, we identify a meaningful TrPL acquisition window (0-2 μs) and decay cutoff (at 0.01), providing guidance toward standardized TrPL characterization protocols. The proposed framework provides a fast and quantitative approach for disentangling complex recombination pathways. Further, this work represents a significant step toward data-driven analysis of perovskite semiconductor kinetics.

papers.abstract_en: Motion sickness (MS) is a common response to conflicting motion signals and can cause nausea, dizziness, malaise, and reduced activity. Sound can lessen MS, but how auditory cues influence the brain circuits that generate these symptoms is unclear. Here we show, using a repeated rotation paradigm in male mice, that a brief anticipatory tone reduces MS-like responses. We identify Cerebellin-2-expressing (Cbln2+) glutamatergic neurons in the medial vestibular nuclei (MVN), a brainstem center for balance signals, as key drivers of these responses. These neurons act through two separable outputs: a projection to the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray that promotes MS-like behavior, and a projection to the nucleus of the solitary tract that contributes to nausea-related aversion, likely through the parabrachial nucleus. Anticipatory tone cues recruit an inhibitory pathway from the central amygdala to suppress Cbln2+ MVN neurons. These findings reveal how auditory prediction can dampen vestibular circuits that drive MS.

papers.abstract_en: 2D magnetic semiconductors, which intrinsically couple a rich landscape of magnetic orders with tightly bound electron-hole pairs (excitons), present an exciting platform to investigate the interplay between optical and magnetic phenomena at the atomic scale. In such systems, the strength of magneto-optical effects determines how deeply the magnetic properties can be revealed. Here, we report the observation of remarkably strong magneto-optical effects in the 2D magnetic semiconductor CrSBr that allow probing its magnetic order with unprecedented sensitivity. By investigating optical transitions above the fundamental exciton energy, we discover massive spectral red- and blueshifts approaching 100 meV under applied magnetic fields - an order of magnitude larger than previously observed magneto-excitonic responses. Our comprehensive magneto-optical experiments, accompanied by detailed DFT calculations, indicate the possible origin of the transitions exhibiting such intriguing behavior. These findings open avenues for exploiting magneto-optical phenomena in newly accessible regimes, enabling novel opto-spintronic applications previously limited by weak magnetic responses.

papers.abstract_en: Tropical cyclone post-landfall decay strongly influences inland hazard exposure, yet most studies assume that environmental change affects storms of different intensities uniformly. Here we identify an intensity-dependent divergence in global trends of tropical cyclone post-landfall decay. Analyzing 885 observed events (1979-2024), we show that strong storms (≥29 m/s) now weaken 18.6% faster after landfall, whereas weak storms persist 14.5% longer inland. These contrasting trends arise from different environmental sensitivities. Weak storms respond primarily to thermodynamic factors, including sea-surface warming, enhanced atmospheric moisture, and increased oceanic influence along storm tracks, all of which favor prolonged inland persistence. In contrast, strong storms are more sensitive to dynamic and land-surface conditions, including faster translation speeds, increasing atmospheric stability, and drier soil, which collectively promote faster decay. Numerical experiments further demonstrate that weaker storms respond more strongly to thermodynamic enhancement, whereas stronger storms are more vulnerable to dynamic disruption. These results challenge uniform-response assumptions in tropical cyclone risk assessment, forging a dual-threat landscape: intensifying coastal impacts from faster-decaying strong storms alongside expanding inland risks from increasingly persistent weak systems. Our findings reveal pronounced intensity-dependent heterogeneity in tropical cyclones, urging refined hazard assessment and adaptation for vulnerable and unprepared regions worldwide.

papers.abstract_en: Opportunities remain to leverage population structure in large scale genomic studies for additional insight. Admixture mapping (AM) identifies loci where disease risk differs by ancestral background, offering a complementary strategy to genome-wide association studies (GWAS) in admixed populations. We performed a systematic comparison of AM and GWAS across over 800 clinical phenotypes in Hispanic/Latino (HL) and African American (AA) participants from the BioMe biobank. We developed a well-calibrated AM pipeline tailored to the local ancestry structure of HL (N = 14,876) and AA (N = 8,819). While GWAS identified a greater number of significant associations, AM revealed 77 signals, including 48 not detected by GWAS. AM-tagged variants had higher minor allele frequency and population differentiation (Fst), while GWAS demonstrated higher odds ratios, underscoring the distinct genetic architecture identified by each method. This study emphasizes the importance of applying both GWAS and AM approaches to uncover previously unreported loci in admixed populations.

papers.abstract_en: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) demands high-performance hardware accelerators. Photonic computing with microring resonators (MRRs) has attracted significant interest, but conventional architectures use MRRs primarily as scalar weights, with speed constrained by the resonance linewidth of  ~ 10 GHz. Here, we redefine MRRs as programmable temporal convolution kernels by exploiting their impulse responses, enabling computation beyond the resonance linewidth. A single MRR operating at a symbol rate of 128 Gbaud achieves a computing throughput of 5.12 trillion operations per second (TOPS), representing a 160-fold improvement over scalar weighting. By integrating temporal convolution with wavelength- and space-division multiplexing, we realize a multi-channel MRR convolution engine with 120.8 TOPS throughput and reduce the hardware complexity from O(N2) to O(N), achieving a compute density of 48.05 TOPS/mm2. The framework is experimentally validated through optical modulation format identification, network anomaly detection, and image classification, establishing a scalable computing primitive for photonic AI accelerators.

papers.abstract_en: Antibiotic resistance has become a critical public health problem, rendering many antibiotics ineffective. In particular, the evolution of extended-spectrum β-lactamases (ESBLs) threatens β-lactams, the cornerstone of bacterial infection treatment. We investigated the evolution of Escherichia coli TEM-1 β-lactamase into ESBLs by constructing a combinatorially complete library of all 55,296 TEM-1 variants from 18 clinical mutations across 13 residues. We obtained over 9,000,000 fitness measurements under native (ampicillin) and non-native (aztreonam) selection. Graph-theoretic and epistatic analyses revealed that ampicillin selection produced weak epistasis and predictable evolutionary trajectories, whereas aztreonam selection induced extensive higher-order epistasis, increasing phenotypic unpredictability. Machine learning identified interpretable epistatic rules shaping these landscapes. Evolutionary statistics, including direct coupling analysis and latent generative landscapes, showed that top-performing ESBL variants followed conserved epistatic patterns observed in natural β-lactamases. Our integrated experimental-computational framework provides a foundation for predicting ESBL evolution and quantifying mutational contributions to ESBL variants.

papers.abstract_en: Understanding and controlling phase transitions is fundamental to physics and central to many technological revolutions. There is currently strong interest in materials with coupled structural and electronic phase transitions, where controlling the transition plasticity naturally yields built-in memory, key for emulating neurons and synapses in neuromorphic technologies. Here, operando coherent Bragg X-ray diffraction is used to study the evolution of the nano-domain distribution at the micron-scale in neuromorphic devices made from the archetypal Mott insulator vanadium dioxide. Electrical switching leads to nano-domain reconfiguration over thousands of seconds and a jamming transition. Repetitive above-threshold currents plastically drive the system into a jammed/glassy state where switching is deterministic. Sub-threshold currents erase the short-term memory defined by the nano-domain distribution, recovering stochastic switching, thus offering a path for in-device learning. These results highlight the importance of nanoscale physics in phase transitions, even for macroscopic devices, and offer guidance for future device operation.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: FGFR2b is an appealing therapeutic biomarker in gastric and gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma, but first-line bemarituzumab development ended despite a statistically positive FORTITUDE-101 primary overall-survival analysis. This review uses the bemarituzumab programme to examine what a clinically useful FGFR2b biomarker must capture and how those requirements change across therapeutic modalities. RECENT FINDINGS: FGFR2b protein overexpression and FGFR2 genomic alteration identify related but non-equivalent populations. Assay threshold, specimen age and spatial heterogeneity affect apparent expression. Within both FIGHT and FORTITUDE-101, OS hazard-ratio estimates moved toward the null at later data cutoffs, although results should not be interpreted across trials as a single trend. A phase 3 trial on a nivolumab-containing backbone was stopped for inadequate efficacy according to sponsor communications. Neither phase 3 study has yet been fully reported in a peer-reviewed publication. Emerging FGFR2-directed agents may require modality-specific biomarkers beyond the original bemarituzumab staining threshold. Prospective development should evaluate modality-matched biomarkers: accessible surface protein and spatial distribution for antibodies, activating genomic changes for kinase inhibitors, and antigen density, internalisation, trafficking and payload sensitivity for antibody-drug conjugates. These remain research priorities rather than validated patient-level treatment rules.
