papers.authors: Nie X, Jiang C, Xiayidan A, Zeng D, Gu Y, Zhang J, Cai G
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Respiratory Diseases, Changzheng Hospital, the Second Military Medical University, Shanghai, 200433, PR, C…
papers.results: 天然抗原下抗GPIIb/IIIa抗体阳性40例（30.77%），抗GPIb/IX抗体阳性17例（13.08%）；SDS处理后反应性分别消失于13例与2例，提示为纯GP复合物依赖性抗体。复合物依赖性抗体患者血小板聚集明显受损；聚集受损患者血清使供者血小板CD62P表达更低（P=0.0323）；血小板去唾液酸化与凋亡在组间无显著差异；与血小板聚集受损相关的抗体亦与更高的SMOG出血指数相关（P<0.001）。
papers.authors_conclusion: GP复合物依赖性与非依赖性自身抗体在慢性ITP中代表功能上不同的抗体谱；复合物依赖性自身抗体显著损害血小板聚集，携带此类功能活性抗体的患者表现出更严重的出血相关症状；功能性抗体表征可能改善出血风险评估并支持更个体化的管理。
papers.ai_note: ①GP复合物依赖性亚组样本量极小（13例与2例），关联估计不稳定，摘要未给任何效应量与置信区间，仅给P值；②CD62P的P=0.0323属边缘显著，未说明多重比较校正；③主要功能学结论“聚集明显受损”仅定性描述，缺乏聚集率数值与统计量；④去唾液酸化、凋亡为阴性结果但无数据呈现；⑤横断面设计无法确立自身抗体功能与出血严重度之间的因果或预测价值，摘要提出的“改善出血风险评估”缺乏预测模型构建与验证；⑥出血关联用SMOG指数，是否校正血小板计数等混杂未交代——信息不足。

pico.p: 130例慢性免疫性血小板减少症（ITP）患者血清；供者血小板用于体外功能实验
pico.ic: 以SDS介导的GP复合物变性区分GP复合物依赖性 vs 非依赖性自身抗体（间接流式微球法检测抗GP抗体），比较两组血小板聚集、活化（CD62P）、凋亡与去唾液酸化，并分析其与临床出血（SMOG出血指数）的关联

papers.reason: 为慢性ITP提供“抗体功能表型（复合物依赖性）—血小板聚集缺陷—出血严重度”的机制-临床关联证据，可作为出血风险分层研究的假说来源与体外功能实验方法学参考；与胸外科/胸部肿瘤业务关联度低，主要价值在于围手术期血小板功能与出血风险评估的背景知识。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Platelet membrane glycoproteins (GPs) serve as key autoantigens in immune thrombocytopenia (ITP). Autoantibodies target linear or conformational epitopes of intact GP complexes, yet the distinct contributions in platelet injury remain unclear. OBJECTIVES: To determine how GP-complex-dependent and GP-complex-independent autoantibodies affect platelet aggregation, activation, apoptosis and desialylation in chronic ITP, and to assess their associations with clinical bleeding. METHODS: Serum anti-GP antibodies from 130 patients with chronic ITP were measured using an indirect flow cytometry microbeads assay. Sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS)-mediated denaturation of GP complexes was used to distinguish the two antibody subtypes. Platelet aggregation, activation, apoptosis and desialylation were assessed by microaggregation, CD62P expression, mitochondrial membrane potential, and lectin-binding assays, respectively. RESULTS: Anti-GPIIb/IIIa and anti-GPIb/IX antibodies were detected against native antigens in 40 (30.77%) and 17 (13.08%) patients, respectively. Following SDS treatment, antibody reactivity was abolished in 13 and 2 patients respectively, indicating exclusively GP-complex-dependent antibodies. Patients with complex-dependent antibodies exhibited markedly impaired platelet aggregation. Sera from patients with impaired aggregation induced lower CD62P expression in donor platelets (P=0.0323), whereas platelet desialylation and apoptosis did not differ significantly between groups. Antibodies associated with impaired platelet aggregation were also linked to higher Skin, visible Mucosae, Organs, and Gradation of Severity (SMOG) bleeding index (P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: GP-complex-dependent and -independent autoantibodies represent functionally distinct antibody profiles in chronic ITP. Complex-dependent autoantibodies significantly impaired platelet aggregation, and patients harboring these functionally active antibodies exhibited more severe bleeding-related symptoms. Functional antibody characterization may improve bleeding-risk assessment and support more individualized management.

pico.ic: 干预：CaNAD+-PGB-LiP（CNAPL）高载荷NAD+纳米药物，实现细胞内直接补充NAD+；对照：摘要未明确描述对照设置（隐含未治疗/免疫抑制对照）

papers.reason: 为移植后闭塞性细支气管炎/肺GVHD提供'控制炎症而不增加感染易感性'的临床前概念验证，可作为肺GVHD免疫抑制减量策略与代谢靶点研究的对照基线；与胸外科/胸部肿瘤直接业务关联有限。
papers.abstract_en: Chronic lung graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) remains difficult to treat, and broad immunosuppression increases infection risk. Single-cell profiling of bronchoalveolar lavage from bronchiolitis obliterans lesions revealed collapse of an epithelial nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) metabolic axis with pathogenic immune-epithelial remodeling, nominating NAD+ restoration as an entry point. Because free NAD+ is poorly cell-permeable and rapidly consumed, we engineered CaNAD+-PGB-LiP (CNAPL), a high-payload NAD+ nanomedicine enabling direct intracellular replenishment. In murine allo-HSCT GVHD, CNAPL improved clinical scores and survival, reduced vascular and epithelial injury, and curtailed hyperinflammation and effector overactivation across GVHD target organs. Unlike immunosuppression, CNAPL preserved phagocytosis, NK/NKT cell (natural killer/natural killer T cell) cytotoxicity, and T cell memory. In posttransplant influenza or Klebsiella infection, CNAPL maintained pathogen control without rekindling GVHD, decoupling inflammation control from infection susceptibility. This metabolism-centered, host-directed strategy restores immune-tissue homeostasis and provides a practical translational path for durable lung GVHD control with preserved antimicrobial defense.

papers.abstract_en: The acidic microenvironment in solid tumors is not merely a metabolic byproduct of the Warburg effect but actively promotes disease aggressiveness and treatment failure. Tumor alkalization therapy, which aims to neutralize or alkalinize the TME, has therefore emerged as a promising adjunct to conventional cancer treatments. In this study, we fabricated both SERS nanosensors and microsensors for parallel spatiotemporal monitoring of intracellular pH (pHi) and extracellular pH (pHe) within tumor spheroids derived from three human cancer cell lines: lung adenocarcinoma (H1975), pancreatic cancer (SW1990), and colorectal cancer (SW480). Over a 7-day culture period, distinct pHi and pHe profiles were observed among the different cell types. We then examined the pH modulation elicited by administration of sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3), a clinically employed alkaline agent. Exposure to 75 mM NaHCO3 for 24 h induced a marked elevation of pHe (∼0.78 units) and a modest increment in pHi (∼0.37 units). This integrated nanosensor-microsensor system, which leverages the size effect for precise spatial localization, offers a versatile approach for elucidating the complex interactions within the tumor microenvironment and helps optimize pH-modulating cancer therapies.

papers.abstract_en: Cardiovascular disease remains a major global health burden, and monitoring vascular information is crucial for the management of cardiovascular disease in daily life. However, existing wearable technologies suffer from limitations such as poor signal quality, limited sensing modalities, and low accuracy. Here, we propose a wearable ultrasonic array patch system comprising 64 elements to overcome the above difficulties and be used for tracking blood dynamics and blood pressure fluctuations. Guided by finite-element piezoelectric simulations, the size of the ultrasonic array was designed. Additionally, the patch utilizes a hydrogel material to ensure proper coupling with the skin. Testing revealed that the patch achieves a -6 dB bandwidth of 71% and a peak-to-peak received voltage of 0.22 V. The patch achieves a high spatial resolution of 0.96 mm × 0.60 mm at a detection depth of 15 mm. The system employs two key approaches to acquire physiological information. The first is a multimodal acquisition scheme capable of simultaneously capturing relative blood pressure trends and hemodynamic characteristics. The second is an angle-dependent reduced vector Doppler framework that utilizes multi-angle beams to calculate blood flow vectors. This work builds on existing wearable ultrasound devices and establishes a platform for the continuous assessment and monitoring of vascular hemodynamics.

papers.abstract_en: Background Self-swab enhanced surveillance of respiratory pathogens is an emerging public health tool that could expand the reach of existing surveillance, providing real-time monitoring of circulating pathogens in the community. Methods We conducted a literature search using terms covering self-swabbing, respiratory infection, and surveillance. For inclusion, publications had to describe a study on the use of serial unsupervised self-swabbing for the purpose of tracking the frequency of respiratory infections in the general population. Results We found 42 publications originating from 27 unique studies on self-swab enhanced surveillance for respiratory infection. Twenty-six studies (96%) were conducted in a high-income setting. Eleven studies (41%) included children under the age of 12 years. Most studies involved a central laboratory conducting polymerase chain reaction testing on returned self-swabs which permitted testing for a wide range of pathogens. Among studies reporting the number of invitees, <20% of invited individuals typically agreed to join. In studies requiring regular symptom reporting, adherence was commonly >75%. Adherence rates for self-swab return were more variable (between 42-96%). Eight studies (30%) explored rapid antigen testing which appears to reduce the time taken between symptom onset and test result notification but limits the number of pathogens that can be evaluated compared with polymerase chain reaction testing. Based on our findings we present a list of suggestions to guide future implementation and investigation. Conclusions Further work is needed to characterise self-swab enhanced surveillance approaches that optimise community participation and protocol adherence, generate as close to real-time data as possible, and minimise costs.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Von Willebrand factor (VWF)-mediated platelet adhesion under flow conditions is tightly regulated by intramolecular autoinhibitory interactions, including the interaction between the A1 and A2 domains. Type 2M von Willebrand disease (VWD) is attributed to impaired binding of the A1 domain to platelet glycoprotein Ibα (GPIbα). OBJECTIVES: To investigate the effects of type 2M mutations on A1/A2 interactions and platelet adhesion. METHODS: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were performed to predict the effects of type 2M VWD mutations located at the A1/A2 interface on interdomain interactions. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) and biolayer interferometry (BLI) were used to validate the computational findings. Flow assays were used to evaluate platelet adhesion under flow conditions. RESULTS: MD simulations identified eight reported type 2M mutations clustered at the A1/A2 binding interface. AFM and BLI experiments demonstrated that these mutations generally enhanced A1/A2 interactions. Platelet adhesion assays revealed these mutations impair platelet adhesion through distinct effects, including reduced A1/GPIbα binding and enhanced A1/A2 interaction. S1358N, V1360A, L1361W, K1362T, Y1363C, L1365R, and F1369I directly impaired platelet adhesion to VWF-A1. Notably, E1359K impaired platelet adhesion to isolated VWF-A1 under high shear conditions, whereas under low shear, the mutation markedly reduced platelet adhesion only in the presence of the A2 domain, suggesting a shear- and A2-dependent regulation of platelet adhesion. CONCLUSIONS: Type 2M mutations located at the A1/A2 interface impair platelet adhesion through distinct effects on reduced A1/GPIbα binding and enhanced A1/A2 interaction. This study provides new insight into the regulatory role of the A1/A2 interaction in type 2M VWD.

papers.abstract_en: Pleural and thoracic air-leak complications after hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) are clinically important but underrepresented in broad post-transplant pulmonary reviews. Direct evidence is concentrated in adult allogeneic HCT. In a cohort of 618 adults, clinically significant pleural effusion had a 1-year cumulative incidence of 9.9% (95% confidence interval, 7.7-12.5%). A separate computed tomography-based cohort of 178 first allogeneic HCT recipients reported a day-100 cumulative incidence of 41.0%; these estimates are not directly comparable because the populations, ascertainment methods, endpoints, and follow-up differed. In 50 HCT recipients undergoing thoracentesis, a specific diagnosis was established in 26%, with 5 pneumothoraces and 0 hemothoraces. Thoracic air-leak syndrome is uncommon but carries poor outcomes in reported adult and pediatric series. This focused narrative review distinguishes direct HCT evidence from data extrapolated from hematologic malignancy, general pleural practice, critical care, interventional radiology, and cellular therapy. We organize evaluation by urgency, transplant phase, and radiographic pattern; define chronic graft-versus-host disease serositis as a diagnosis of exclusion; summarize chylothorax and pleural infection management; and provide procedure-specific safety considerations for thoracentesis, small-bore drainage, indwelling pleural catheters, intrapleural enzyme therapy, and pleural biopsy. No prospective HCT-specific trials validate these procedural pathways. Clinicians should therefore use ultrasound or image guidance; apply procedure-specific rather than uniform hemostatic thresholds; and integrate infection risk, platelet trajectory, anticoagulant exposure, oxygenation, operator setting, and expected benefit. The two clinical frameworks presented are proposed and non-validated.

papers.abstract_en: Dynamic electrocardiographic (ECG) monitoring has become an indispensable tool in clinical diagnosis and non-invasive monitoring. However, its front-end sensing component, ECG electrodes, still have issues such as long-term stability and dynamic artifacts, which limit its application in high-reliability scenarios. Therefore, developing highly biocompatible ECG electrodes, reducing or stabilizing contact impedance, and eliminating relative sliding during movement are of utmost importance. Here, a textile-array electrode (TAE) was integrated with a micropillar array on the semi-interpenetrating network (SIN) textile, which was woven from core-sheath hydrogel fibers. Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene)-poly(styrenesulfonate) was used as a conductive material to minimize electrolyte content and ensure high biocompatibility after continuous monitoring (24 h). Micropillar arrays with a larger contact area than Holter electrodes were applied to reduce contact impedance by 85%. Polyester filaments were served as the core layer and woven with cotton to stabilize electron density and resistance, achieving strain-insensitive characteristics (∼0.02%). TAE was embedded into the garment to capture precise ECG signals with a signal-to-noise ratio of 21.56 dB (similar to resting state) during dynamic monitoring, and these signals can be used to analyze RR intervals for heart rate variability. This work is conducive to more efficient, precise, and personalized health management solutions and promotes the development of intelligent medical technology.

papers.abstract_en: Engineering functional bone scaffolds can be enhanced by integrating biologically instructive nanoscale surface features (e.g., nanotopography and nanoroughness), micro-scale geometric cues (e.g., curvature and porosity), and macro-scale mechanical properties (e.g., bulk stiffness); however, these length scales are often optimized independently. Here, we present a multiscale design framework combining additive manufacturing of triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) gyroid scaffolds with plasma-assisted nanoscale surface engineering to regulate osteogenesis. Controlled variation in strut thickness generates distinct architectural regimes with coupled changes in curvature, porosity, and compressive modulus, recapitulating key aspects of trabecular bone mechanics. Micro-computed tomography confirms trabecular bone-like features, while finite element modeling and compression testing reveal that thinner architectures (0.6 mm) exhibit curvature-preserving geometry and distributed stress profiles favorable for cellular interaction. A low-temperature plasma electroless reduction (PER) strategy enables controlled silver nanoparticle (AgNP) deposition, while polydopamine (PDA) ensures uniform, cytocompatible coatings. Notably, PDA-AgNP-functionalized 0.6 mm scaffolds exhibit enhanced cytoskeletal organization, mineralization, and osteogenic gene expression, accompanied by elevated reactive oxygen species (ROS) and YAP/TAZ-associated transcriptional activity. These findings support cross-scale coupling of architecture and nanoscale biointerfaces as a design framework for osteogenic scaffolds.

papers.abstract_en: The development of reactive oxygen species (ROS)-scavenging materials for biomedical applications has been constrained by the difficulty associated with achieving simultaneously broad-spectrum scavenging efficiency and acceptable biosafety. To date, ceria/nanoceria systems have been explored for this purpose; however, they suffer from limited cerium-atom utilization. Inspired by the atom-economy concept of single-atom catalysis, we report a cerium-based molecular-cage strategy for treating oxidative stress-driven atherosclerosis (AS). It involves mixed-valent cerium ions (Ce3+/Ce4+) that are stably confined within tailored molecular cages and that mimic the cooperation between oxygen vacancies and cerium redox cycling in CeO2. This endows the four representative cages of this study with an ability to scavenge superoxide anion (O2•-), hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), and hydroxyl radical (•OH). Their catalytic function can be readily modulated through the ROS-responsive release of the molecular cages at local lesion sites. This capability was found to alleviate oxidative stress and associated inflammation, as inferred from the finding that a lead cerium cage incorporated into a biocompatible nanoparticle reduces the progression of AS in a mouse model. A reduction in plaque lipid deposition, macrophage accumulation, necrotic core formation, and MMP-9-associated matrix was seen.

papers.abstract_en: High-pressure drug-coated balloon (HP@DCB) angioplasty enhances vascular drug delivery by overcoming the limitations of passive diffusion-based conventional noncompliant DCB (NC@DCB) systems. We developed a dual-layer HP balloon catheter composed of an outer Nylon 12 layer and an inner Pebax 7233 layer, and evaluated its feasibility and therapeutic efficacy as a paclitaxel (PTX)-coated platform. Shellac-based PTX coating was uniformly applied to HP@DCB and NC@DCB, and coating thickness, drug amount, release behavior, and mechanical properties were compared. Pressure-assisted drug penetration was assessed in a vascular-mimicking agarose gel phantom using fluorescent PTX and confocal microscopy. In vivo efficacy was evaluated in a balloon injury-induced rabbit iliac artery stenosis model using angiography, optical coherence tomography (OCT), histology, immunohistochemistry, and immunofluorescence examinations. Drug amount, coating thickness, and sustained drug release did not differ between groups. The mechanical robustness in HP@DCB was significantly greater than that in NC@DCB. HP@DCB produced significantly greater penetration depth and fluorescence-positive area, indicating enhanced pressure-assisted drug transfer. HP@DCB resulted in superior luminal patency, reduced neointimal hyperplasia, and favorable biological responses compared with that in NC@DCB and the sham control. These findings support DCB use based on a dual-layered HP balloon platform as a promising next-generation strategy for stenotic vascular lesion treatment.

papers.abstract_en: As humans spend most of their time indoors, they are continuously exposed to an array of indoor air pollutants. While exposure to individual indoor air pollutants may often occur at low levels, cumulative exposure to indoor air pollutants contributes substantially to the human exposome. Chronic inhalation of indoor air pollutants has been associated with multiple respiratory diseases, including asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and respiratory infections. In this study, the cellular effects of an acute indoor dust exposure using a three-dimensional airway epithelial model were investigated. Bronchial epithelial cells (16HBE14o-) were cultured as spheroids and exposed to reference indoor dust (SRM 2585; 0-200 µg/mL) for 24 h. Metabolic activity, intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, inflammatory cytokine secretion, and secretome profiles were assessed. Indoor dust exposure did not induce morphological alterations or significant reductions in metabolic activity. Instead, a concentration-dependent increase in intracellular ROS was observed. Cytokine analysis revealed selective cytokine modulation, while untargeted proteomics identified limited changes in individual protein abundance. Instead, pathway-level analyses revealed enrichment of epithelial differentiation-related pathways. Overall, these findings suggest that a 24 h indoor dust exposure may elicit subtle cellular responses rather than overt cytotoxicity or inflammatory activation. This study highlights the applicability of integrating functional, immunological, and proteomics-based approaches with 3D airway models to investigate cellular responses to complex environmental particle mixtures. However, direct extrapolation to human exposure scenarios is limited by uncertainties regarding effective cellular dose, particle localization and environmental representativeness. Therefore, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory, hypothesis-generating observations.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: Measles is among the most transmissible human infections, yet direct capture of measles virus from an infected person's exhaled breath has not been described. We assessed whether measles virus RNA can be detected from exhaled breath using facemask sampling (FMS). METHODS: We studied a 23-year-old unvaccinated woman with laboratory-confirmed measles (throat-swab RT-qPCR positive on day 5 post symptom onset). From day 10 post symptom onset, longitudinal sampling was performed for six consecutive days with duplicate specimens collected at each timepoint from the throat, face, cutaneous lesions and exhaled breath using a surgical mask fitted with polyvinyl alcohol sampling strips (FMS). Dissolved mask strips and swab eluates underwent RNA extraction followed by RT-qPCR targeting measles nucleoprotein and haemagglutinin genes, with human RNase P as a sample adequacy control. Quantification was derived from nucleoprotein-gene standards and normalised per strip or per 100 μL of swab eluate. RESULTS: Measles virus RNA was consistently detected in exhaled breath captured by FMS and remained >10ˆ4 genome copies per sampling strip despite sampling beginning 10 days after symptom onset. During FMS collection, the participant reported no respiratory symptoms and did not vocalise. RNA kinetics differed by sampling site: throat and facial swabs increased even after complete rash resolution, whereas cutaneous-lesion swabs yielded comparatively low RNA levels. FMS kinetics diverged from throat swabs over time, suggesting distinct patterns of virus emission across compartments. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides the first empirical evidence that measles virus RNA can be captured directly from the exhaled breath of an individual with measles. Although RNA detection does not confirm infectious virus, persistent high-level exhaled RNA supports FMS as a practical, non-invasive tool to study measles respiratory emission and may inform understanding of transmission and the duration of potential contagiousness. Empirical sampling of different respiratory compartments may help refine infection-prevention guidance during resurgent outbreaks.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Conventional burn dressings maintain a moist wound environment and reduce infection but do not directly counteract the sustained oxidative stress and inflammation of the burn wound bed. Cerium dioxide (CeO2) nanoparticles possess redox-based antioxidant activity, motivating their incorporation into a resorbable dressing. This study aimed to fabricate and preliminarily evaluate CeO2-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanofiber dressings for burn wound healing. METHODS: CeO2-loaded and pristine PLGA nanofibers were produced by electrospinning and characterized for fiber morphology, elemental composition, tensile properties, wettability, water uptake, and in vitro cytocompatibility. Wound healing was assessed in a full-thickness rat burn model over 28 days, with histological analysis at days 7 and 28. RESULTS: CeO2-incorporated nanofibers showed a smaller average fiber diameter (159.8 ± 97.6 nm) than pristine PLGA nanofibers (267.9 ± 146.3 nm). CeO2 incorporation reduced tensile strength, although all fibers retained good elongation (> 50%) before fracture. In vivo, the CeO2-loaded nanofibers produced a transient reduction in wound area that was significantly greater than the control at days 14 and 21 and greater than pristine PLGA at day 14 (p < 0.05); by day 28, wound areas had converged and the differences among groups were no longer statistically significant. Histological analysis showed earlier collagen deposition and no adverse tissue response. CONCLUSION: CeO2-loaded PLGA nanofiber dressings are biocompatible and can accelerate the intermediate phase of burn wound closure in a rat model. Because the CeO2 redox state, CeO2 release, and in vivo antioxidant mechanisms were not directly measured, the improvement cannot yet be causally attributed to CeO2, and further mechanistic studies are required.

papers.abstract_en: The SARS-CoV-2 Omicron subvariant JN.4 harbors a unique A475V substitution within the receptor binding domain (RBD) but exhibits limited expansion compared to its parallel descendant JN.1. Here, we investigate how hydrophobic remodeling within RBD large loop (residues 475-490) modulates receptor engagement and spike function. Cryo-electron microscopy reveals that A475V induces local remodeling of the receptor-binding motif (RBM) and alters the RBD-ACE2 interaction geometry. Local refinement revealed that the bulky valine substitution disrupts the local interaction network surrounding residue 475, resulting in a 3.5-fold reduction in ACE2-binding affinity compared with BA.2.86. In contrast to the L455S substitution in JN.1, which primarily alters the receptor-binding interface, A475V within the flexible large loop influences both local loop conformation and global spike conformational properties. Systematic mutagenesis identifies A475 and F486 as functionally constrained hydrophobic residues that preserve the structural framework of ACE2 engagement despite extensive sequence variation within the surrounding loop. Together with molecular dynamics simulations and functional assays, our findings establish the RBD 475-490 large loop as a structurally plastic yet functionally constrained element that balances receptor recognition, conformational stability, and antigenic diversification. These results provide a mechanistic framework for understanding region-specific evolutionary constraints that shape SARS-CoV-2 RBD adaptation.

papers.abstract_en: Auranofin, an FDA-approved oral anti-rheumatic drug, was previously shown by our group to restrict Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2) replication and pathology in preclinical models. Here, we systematically characterized its mechanism of action (MOA) through biochemical drug-protein interactions, cell-based mechanistic assays, and preclinical efficacy studies. Auranofin directly binds and inhibits SARS-CoV-2 MPro while simultaneously targeting multiple stages of the viral life cycle, disrupting endosomal trafficking, suppressing Spike S1/S2 proteolytic processing, impairing syncytia formation, and attenuating NF-κB-driven proinflammatory signaling. In cell culture, Auranofin demonstrated robust synergy with Remdesivir but competed with the MPro inhibitor Nirmatrelvir, informing rational combination design. In mice infected with the SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant, the oral combination of Auranofin and the Remdesivir prodrug GS-621763 outperformed monotherapy, markedly reducing viral replication, inflammatory cytokine responses, and lung pathology, and improving clinical outcomes. These findings establish a multi-target antiviral MOA of Auranofin and provide a mechanistic rationale for an all-oral antiviral combination regimen against COVID-19.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is a common and medically refractory neurological disorder with a complex pathogenesis. Blood-brain barrier (BBB) dysfunction is a key pathogenic factor. As a multifunctional protein, TGM2 has been shown to participate in vascular homeostasis, metabolic pathway regulation, and immune-inflammatory responses. This study aimed to systematically investigate the expression pattern, core functions, and molecular regulatory mechanisms of TGM2 in TLE, and to clarify its clinical value. METHODS: Temporal cortex tissue and plasma samples from drug-resistant TLE patients and control subjects were collected, alongside kainic acid (KA)-induced epileptic mouse models. Single-cell RNA sequencing was adopted to identify TGM2's cell-specific expression pattern, and qPCR, Western blot and ELISA validated its expression levels. With endothelial cell-specific TGM2 conditional knockout mice, in vivo experiments assessed seizure severity and BBB permeability through behavioral observation, intracranial local field potential (LFP) recording and Evans blue (EB) assay. In vitro siRNA-mediated TGM2 knockdown in brain microvascular endothelial cells verified endothelial functional changes. Metabolomics, RNA-seq, nucleocytoplasmic separation, immunofluorescence and molecular docking were used to clarify regulatory mechanisms, and intercellular communication networks were constructed to analyze ligand-receptor interactions. RESULTS: Results indicated that endothelial TGM2 was significantly downregulated in TLE patients and epileptic mice. Endothelial TGM2 deficiency aggravated recurrent seizures, increased BBB permeability, impaired endothelial function, and reduced the expression of tight junction protein CLDN5. Mechanistically, TGM2 positively regulated sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) synthesis. Reduced S1P production abolished the inhibition of RelA nuclear translocation, thereby activating downstream inflammatory genes and triggering endothelial inflammation. Molecular docking confirmed the direct binding between S1P and RelA. Furthermore, TGM2 deficiency remodels endothelial-neuron-microglia communication and disrupts neural circuit homeostasis. CONCLUSIONS: This study establishes a link between TGM2 and BBB function, metabolic pathways, and intercellular communication in TLE, providing an experimental basis for developing TLE therapeutic strategies targeting this pathway.

papers.abstract_en: AbstractHuman adenoviruses (HAdVs) are common respiratory pathogens that cause severe, life-threatening infections in immunocompromised individuals and children. Despite their medical importance, no clinically approved antiviral drugs exist. Here, we showed that 4H30, a 4-branched human defensin peptide, exhibited broad-spectrum antiviral activity against multiple HAdV subtypes in A549 and Calu-3 cells with negligible cytotoxicity and a high barrier to viral resistance in A549 cells. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that 4H30 exhibited a unique dual mechanism of action: direct virucidal activity through capsid disruption and endosomal trapping by impairing protein VI-mediated membrane penetration. Notably, 4H30 remained effective against HAdV-3 in human respiratory organoids and against HAdV-2 and HAdV-5 in an immunosuppressed hamster model, significantly reducing viral replication and disease-associated pathology. These findings demonstrate that 4H30 can inhibit multiple HAdVs through a novel mechanism, offering a new therapeutic avenue against HAdV infections.

papers.abstract_en: Legionella pneumophila is the causative agent of Legionnaires' disease, an accidental and severe form of pneumonia. The replication of L. pneumophila within alveolar macrophages requires the Dot/Icm type IV secretion system that translocates more than 330 bacterial effector proteins into the infected host cell. Many Dot/Icm effectors possess eukaryotic-like domains and manipulate host processes by functional mimicry. However, only a minority of effectors have been fully characterized. Redundancy among effector protein activities and host targets has complicated functional characterization of individual effector proteins. To explore the collective impact of Dot/Icm effectors on host cell processes, we created a library of 14 L. pneumophila genomic mutant strains lacking effector-rich regions (a total of 85 effector genes deleted) and used the multi-deletion mutants to interrogate host-pathogen interactions. While none of the mutants exhibited a defect in intracellular replication in THP-1 macrophages, several were attenuated in amoebae, including a mutant lacking a predicted amino acid transporter. In THP-1 cells, we observed that wild-type L. pneumophila 130b triggered a strong inflammatory and cellular stress transcriptional response in macrophages, whereas six mutants displayed reduced interferon signalling and one mutant displayed a marked decrease in the global expression of host heat shock response (HSR) genes. Through the creation of further sub-deletions, we found that the Dot/Icm effector kinase LegK4 was responsible for induction of the host HSR via the canonical transcription factor heat shock factor 1 (HSF1). Infection of THP-1 macrophages deficient in HSF1 revealed a potential role for the host HSR in the early stages of L. pneumophila infection. Together, these results reinforce the utility of multi-gene deletions to identify Dot/Icm effector phenotypes and the importance of the host HSR to L. pneumophila infection.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: After a year of quiescence, SARS-CoV-2 activity increased rapidly in Hong Kong since June 2026. We sought to characterize the genomic profile of SARS-CoV-2 driving this COVID-19 surge in Hong Kong and to examine the global dissemination of the identified circulating lineages. METHODS: We performed SARS-CoV-2 whole-genome sequencing on archived respiratory specimens collected at Queen Mary Hospital, Hong Kong, between January 2025 and July 2026. Viral lineages were assigned via Nextclade. Global SARS-CoV-2 metadata downloaded from GISAID as of July 2026 were analyzed to track global evolutionary trends. RESULTS: Among 615 successfully sequenced strains, the XDV descendant NB.1.8.1 was the predominant lineage. Between April and July 2026, NB.1.8.1 descendants accounted for 95.6% (108/113) of sequenced strains, dominated by PQ.16.1.1 (81.5%). Spike substitutions 420N and 478 T emerged rapidly. While 478 T increased gradually throughout 2025, 420N emerged in April 2026 and reached 98.0% by June-July 2026. Strains harboring 420N-478 T dual substitution arose independently across distinct NB.1.8.1 lineages, accounting for 94.4% (102/108) of NB.1.8.1 descendants in Hong Kong during this period. Globally, the prevalence of NB.1.8.1 strains with 420N-478 T dual substitution increased from <1% before April 2026 to 50.7% by mid-July 2026, with the highest prevalence observed in Southeast Asia and Australia. CONCLUSIONS: The 2026 COVID-19 surge in Hong Kong was driven by NB.1.8.1 descendants harboring spike 420N and 478 T substitutions. The rapid worldwide expansion of these dual-substitution lineages highlights their competitive growth advantage and underscores the need for continued global genomic surveillance.

papers.abstract_en: Biobank-scale imaging-genomic cohorts enable genome-wide association studies (GWASs) of organ structure and function. Traditional approaches rely on expert-defined image-derived phenotypes (IDPs), which capture only a fraction of the biological variation in high-content images. Powered by artificial intelligence, self-supervised learning (SSL) learns representations directly from intrinsic image structures, creating scalable, data-driven traits. Here, we review the technical frameworks and challenges of SSL-based imaging genetics and their applications in brain MRI, cardiac MRI, and retinal imaging. Early studies suggest that these data-driven approaches can complement traditional IDPs and may expand the phenotypic space available for discovery of heritable imaging traits, although broader validation across cohorts, ancestries, scanners, and imaging protocols remains needed.

papers.abstract_en: Real-time, continuous monitoring of large peptide and protein biomarkers has transformative potential for personalized medicine but is hindered by the rapid degradation of affinity-based sensors in complex biofluids. While physical barriers such as size-exclusion membranes can mitigate biofouling, they also exclude the high-molecular-weight proteins to be measured, creating a fundamental paradox for sensor design. Here, we present a solution to this stability-fouling trade-off: a "mixed charge" monolayer interface that confers multi-week fouling resistance without relying on physical filtration. By incorporating compact amine- and carboxyl-terminations onto 8-carbon alkyl thiolates, we engineered a surface that mimics zwitterionic hydration while preserving the dense molecular packing and intermolecular forces required for long-term monolayer stability. This architecture extends the operational lifetime of electrochemical aptamer sensors to 14 days in whole serum. Sensors targeting the small molecule cortisol retained ∼80% of their initial analyte response signal gain, while those targeting the protein platelet-derived growth factor bb (PDGF-bb) preserved nearly 100% of their analyte response signaling capacity over the two-week period. These findings demonstrate a generalized, membrane-free platform capable of robust, multi-week molecular monitoring of larger peptides and proteins.

papers.authors: Lee K, Jung JH, Lee J, Lee JW, Jeong CH, Kim EJ, Lee S

papers.authors_conclusion: Ketamine is a potentially valuable opioid-sparing adjunct for selected patients with cancer-related pain and may also address comorbid depressive symptoms. Its putative direct anti-tumor and immunomodulatory actions remain predominantly preclinical and context dependent and should not currently guide oncologic treatment decisions. Appropriately powered clinical studies should define patient selection, dose and route, duration, safety, immune consequences, and long-term oncologic outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: To synthesize current evidence on ketamine for cancer-related pain and its intersecting psychiatric, anti-tumor, and immunomodulatory actions, emphasizing mechanisms, clinical relevance, and uncertainties relevant to oncology. RECENT FINDINGS: Ketamine provides analgesia primarily through non-competitive antagonism of N-methyl-D-aspartate receptors and additional effects on excitatory, inhibitory, and opioid-related signaling. In patients with refractory cancer pain, it may be a useful adjunct to opioid-based multimodal analgesia and may reduce opioid requirements; however, clinical evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. Its rapid antidepressant effects may be relevant to the reciprocal burden of pain and depressive symptoms in cancer. Preclinical studies report antiproliferative, pro-apoptotic, and ferroptosis-associated effects across several tumor models, involving phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B/mechanistic target of rapamycin, extracellular signal-regulated kinase, and non-coding RNA-associated pathways. These findings are not uniform: breast cancer models have suggested potentially pro-metastatic effects. Immune effects are likewise dose-, context-, and perioperative-setting dependent, with reports of anti-inflammatory, immunosuppressive, and neutral effects. Ketamine is a potentially valuable opioid-sparing adjunct for selected patients with cancer-related pain and may also address comorbid depressive symptoms. Its putative direct anti-tumor and immunomodulatory actions remain predominantly preclinical and context dependent and should not currently guide oncologic treatment decisions. Appropriately powered clinical studies should define patient selection, dose and route, duration, safety, immune consequences, and long-term oncologic outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: Intestinal epithelial integrity is essential for host defense, yet how epithelial junctional scaffolds coordinate antimicrobial immunity remains unclear. We show that the long GEF-H1 isoforms (mouse Arhgef2-207; human ARHGEF2-219) localize to adherens junctions in polarized epithelial cells through interactions with actin and Nectin-3, whereas the shorter Arhgef2-201 isoform localizes to tight junctions. Conditional deletion of epithelial Arhgef2-207 induces Arhgef2-201 expression, disrupts barrier integrity, activates autophagy, and causes small-intestinal inflammation. In human intestinal organoids, Listeria monocytogenes selectively depletes junction-associated ARHGEF2-219, triggering a switch to ARHGEF2-201 and RhoA- and STING-mediated autophagic signaling. This transition coincides with loss of the Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase and epithelial polarity. Here we show that a pathogen-induced ARHGEF2 isoform switch links junctional perturbation to autophagic responses and immune activation, revealing a mechanism that couples barrier disruption to cell-intrinsic antimicrobial defense.

papers.abstract_en: Pulmonary fibrosis is a common and often fatal outcome of fibrosing interstitial lung diseases, characterized by progressive extracellular matrix deposition, destruction of alveolar architecture and irreversible loss of respiratory function. Although fibroblast activation and epithelial dysfunction are central to disease pathogenesis, fibrosis cannot be adequately explained by mesenchymal dysregulation alone. Rather, it represents a failure of multicellular repair regulation, in which immune cells, fibroblasts and epithelial populations reciprocally reshape cellular states, tissue niches and disease trajectories. Early innate immune responses amplify epithelial injury while simultaneously initiating provisional repair; however, when injury persists, these transient programmes fail to resolve and become stabilized into chronic profibrotic circuits involving monocyte-derived macrophages, dysfunctional T cells, inflammatory fibroblasts and matrix-producing myofibroblasts. Recent single-cell, spatial transcriptomic and lineage-tracing studies have revealed discrete cellular states, including SPP1⁺ scar-associated macrophages, inflammatory fibroblasts, CTHRC1⁺ myofibroblasts and tertiary-lymphoid-structure-associated stromal cells, that assemble multicellular, stage-specific and microanatomically restricted fibrotic niches. Collectively, these findings support a model in which soluble mediators, extracellular matrix mechanics, metabolic rewiring and immune-regulatory signalling cooperate to establish self-reinforcing stromal-immune circuits. In this Review, we synthesize current evidence for bidirectional immune-fibroblast crosstalk in pulmonary fibrosis, focusing on macrophage and T cell programmes, fibroblast-mediated immune regulation, spatiotemporal niche remodelling, mechanistic signalling networks, experimental models and therapeutic opportunities. We propose that progressive fibrosis reflects the spatiotemporal locking of pathological epithelial-immune-stromal circuits, a framework that may explain the limited efficacy of broad anti-inflammatory therapies in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and guide the development of more precise, stage-specific and combinatorial antifibrotic strategies.

papers.abstract_en: Measurements from whole blood remain challenging with plasmonic techniques, especially for point-of-care (POC) measurements where infrastructure is limited. To address this need, we developed a portable POC surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assay for rapid ferritin quantification from whole blood that uses a lateral flow-based sample preparation strip to collect an eluate from whole blood. The concept is shown with clinical samples for monitoring iron deficiency anemia (IDA), a prevalent global health concern considered with care by blood banks, for which rapid POC quantification has yet to be achieved. The SPR assay detected ferritin concentrations in the ng/mL range from whole blood in 30 min, sufficient to discriminate concentrations at the clinically relevant threshold for IDA. Measurements from eluted blood showed good agreement with centrifuged serum and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) results, allowing clear classification between deficient and normal ferritin levels despite minor variability among clinical samples collected from blood donors. With its portability, short analysis time, and minimal sample preparation, this method demonstrates strong potential for on-site protein sensing, as exemplified for ferritin screening at blood drives with minimal and simple blood preparation, providing a pathway toward future development of point-of-care tools for improved assessment of donor iron status.

papers.abstract_en: Wearable electrochemical biosensors offer direct biochemical readouts but often suffer from enzyme deactivation, biofluid fluctuation, fouling, and calibration drift during prolonged on-body use. Here, we report an ultrathin (∼1.3 μm thick) multimodal sensing system that decouples whole-day physical monitoring from short-term disposable electrochemical calibration. The system integrates stable physical sensors for electrocardiogram, pulse, and temperature acquisition with a detachable electrochemical glucose module that provides personalized calibration labels during initial use. At the material level, the pulse sensor combines an embedded Ag nanowire network with a cracked Cr/MoO3/Cr/Au layer in an ultrathin polyimide matrix, enabling both strain sensitivity and cyclic stability. The resulting strain sensor shows a gauge factor of 5.49 in the 0-4% strain range, a response time of 55 ms, and durability over 15,000 stretching cycles. The detachable glucose sensor employs a co-crosslinked porous enzymatic matrix to delay active-site saturation, achieving a broad linear range of 0-20 mM. After three days of personalized calibration, a random-forest model using 60 s recordings of electrocardiogram, pulse, and temperature signals yields an overall tolerance-based accuracy of 81.36% and a mean absolute relative difference (MARD) of 9.12%. Furthermore, in individual on-body tracking over one day and 15 days, the glucose predictions achieved an accuracy of at least 80%. This stable-physical-sensing/disposable-electrochemical-calibration architecture provides a practical strategy for personalized glucose prediction while mitigating the long-term instability of wearable electrochemical biosensors.

papers.abstract_en: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) pose a threat to human health. Although receptor specificity, polymerase adaptation, and airway tropism have been studied extensively, it remains unresolved how they combine to shape tropism in airway epithelia. Here, we show that avian IAVs infect ciliated and secretory cells but preferentially bind to ciliated cells because of higher apical α2,3-linked sialic acid levels. As replication levels are comparable between cell types, this translates into overall preference for ciliated cells. Human IAVs also preferentially bind to ciliated cells despite comparable α2,6-linked sialic acid abundance. Instead, they show higher viral RNA and protein levels in secretory cells, linked to their compatibility with human ANP32 proteins and modestly higher ANP32A/B expression in this cell type, resulting in equal infection levels across cell types. Our findings redefine IAV tropism in the human airway as a stage-resolved process shaped by the interplay between apical glycans, viral binding, polymerase cofactor compatibility, and cell-type-specific replication capacity, moving beyond receptor-centric models.

papers.abstract_en: Robotic systems for computed tomography (CT)-guided needle insertion have been developed to address the limitations of conventional manual needle insertion. Thus far, various robotic systems have been clinically implemented, and accumulating evidence has suggested their clinical utility. The evidence has evolved beyond initial feasibility and early clinical experience to include larger observational and comparative studies. These studies have demonstrated high success rates of robot-assisted needle insertion in various CT-guided interventions, including thermal ablation, biopsy, and preoperative localization. Furthermore, an increasing number of comparative studies have demonstrated the advantages of robot-assisted procedures over conventional manual procedures. These advantages include improved needle insertion accuracy and reduced radiation doses to patients and/or physicians. Although most currently available robotic systems are needle-guiding robots designed to align a needle guide with a predetermined insertion trajectory, we have developed a CT-guided needle insertion robot capable of robotic needle advancement via remote control. Clinical studies have demonstrated the feasibility of robotic needle insertion using this system, as well as needle placement accuracy comparable to that of manual procedures, while eliminating radiation exposure to physicians. The integration of artificial intelligence and the implementation of telerobotic interventions are expected to contribute significantly to the further advancement of robotic systems for CT-guided needle insertion. This narrative review summarizes the current clinical implementations and available evidence for robotic systems for CT-guided needle insertion, including our system, and discusses future perspectives in this field.

papers.abstract_en: Uncovering general principles connecting neural circuits to behaviour requires comparative brain analyses across species. To advance these efforts, we developed a standardised workflow and a unified brain atlas platform for the quantitative comparison of neural structures between two teleost larvae, medaka (Oryzias latipes) and zebrafish (Danio rerio). Crucially, the platform seamlessly integrates user-generated image volumes, facilitating quantitative comparisons of anatomical, transcriptional, and functional data across species and laboratories. Utilising these integrated tools, we identified regional anatomical differences and differentially expressed genes between the species. We further demonstrated functionally distinct telencephalic regions in both species that exhibit divergent responses to social stimuli, suggesting an evolutionary divergence in social processing mechanisms. This web-based, interactive atlas platform promotes data exchange and knowledge sharing within the teleost community. Its scalable design permits effortless multi-group contributions, enabling expansion into a continuously growing, globally accessible database.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND & AIMS: Immunosenescence increases the risk of infectious diseases in the aged population. A health issue partially caused by a reduced interferon (IFN)-α response. With zinc playing a crucial role in antiviral immunity and zinc-deficiency being highly prevalent in the elderly, this study examined the association between the age-related decline in IFN-α production and zinc status. The aim of this study was to compare the IFN-α response of young controls to geriatric patients stratified by their zinc status, to examine the zinc dependency of the transcription factor Interferon Regulatory Factor (IRF)3 and to investigate whether short-term zinc supplementation of zinc-deficient elderly can restore the antiviral immune competence. METHODS: 41 young healthy controls (YC) and 75 geriatric patients (O; old) were included. The geriatric cohort was divided into zinc-adequate (O-ZA) and zinc-deficient (O-ZD) subgroups based on the measured serum zinc and dietary zinc intake assessed via a food-questionnaire. Whole blood and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were stimulated with Newcastle Disease Virus (NDV) or Sendai Virus (SDV) for 24 h. The subsequent production of IFN-α was measured by ELISA. In addition, basal protein expression of IRF3 was analysed by Western blot. Patients, identified as zinc-deficient, were supplemented with 10 mg of elemental zinc for about 7 days, followed by repeating the measurements. RESULTS: 71% of the geriatric cohort was identified as zinc-deficient. Although the total geriatric group produced significantly less IFN-α compared to the young controls, the zinc-adequate seniors produced significantly higher levels of IFN-α than the zinc-deficient subgroup. Consistent with these findings, a significantly reduced expression of IRF3 was observed in zinc-deficient patients. Furthermore, a significant positive correlation between zinc status, IRF3 expression and IFN-α production was found. In patients that responded to the supplementation with an increase in serum zinc, this supplementation could also restore the IFN-α production to levels comparable to the zinc-adequate seniors. CONCLUSIONS: The findings indicate that the reduced IFN-α response is not an inevitable part of aging. By reducing the basal availability of IRF3, zinc deficiency builds a molecular barrier that limits the cellular capacity for IFN-α production. However, short-term zinc supplementation can counteract this limitation. Hence, routine assessment and correction of zinc status should be integrated into geriatric care to enhance immune resilience in the aging population.

papers.abstract_en: The RNA modification N6-methyladenosine (m6A) precisely regulates eukaryotic gene expression. The deposition of m6A is governed by chromatin environment, transcription and RNA processing. m6A modifications influence chromatin function and RNA splicing, stability, localization and translation, and enable cellular adaptation to environmental changes. Dysregulation of m6A has been implicated in pathological processes, including neurodegenerative diseases and cancer. In this Review, we dissect the m6A machinery by describing how writers and erasers coordinate m6A deposition and reader proteins translate these modifications into diverse functional outcomes. We illustrate how this dynamic regulatory network orchestrates cellular stress responses, metabolic homeostasis and antitumour immunity, and outline the pathological consequences of m6A dysregulation in brain disorders and cancer. Finally, we highlight translational prospects of m6A biology, including the development of specific small-molecule inhibitors and precise editing technologies, and address the remaining challenges for clinical interventions targeting m6A.

papers.abstract_en: Biological systems face a constantly changing environment and must swiftly respond to stimuli; yet how cells sense and adapt to environmental and physiological cues is incompletely understood. Short-lived proteins can be rapidly induced upon perturbation, enabling swift activation of adaptive cellular responses. Here, leveraging genome-wide data on protein-transcript correlation, we systematically searched for rapid proteolysis substrates whose abundance reflects the activity of the underlying proteolytic machinery. Focusing on the candidate substrate ABHD2, we performed CRISPR-based genetic screens to dissect its degradation. These screens identified TXNDC15 as an essential factor in MARCHF6-mediated ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD). Mechanistically, TXNDC15 supports substrate exit and degradation from the ER via a catalysis-independent mechanism. Loss of TXNDC15 remodels the ER proteome and lipid homeostasis. Together, our work defines a missing component of ERAD and provides a generalizable strategy to decode post-translational regulatory circuits.

papers.abstract_en: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors exploit homologous recombination deficiency, but are limited by hematological toxicity and poor discrimination between PARP1 and PARP2. Because PARP1 drives most antitumor PARylation and trapping, whereas PARP2 contributes to hematopoietic maintenance, selective PARP1 inhibition might widen the therapeutic window. Emerging agents, including saruparib and palacaparib, confirm that strong isoform selectivity can coexist with cellular target engagement, tissue exposure, and antitumor activity. However, biochemical selectivity alone is insufficient. Clinical differentiation requires matched comparisons of efficacy, unbound exposure, trapping, dose intensity, and marrow recovery. PARP1 selectivity remains a promising, but not yet proven, strategy for safer and more durable therapy.

papers.abstract_en: Advances in cystic fibrosis care, particularly highly effective cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator modulator therapies, have transformed disease trajectories for many children and adolescents, improving health and survival. However, advanced disease, symptom and treatment burden, psychosocial distress, and uncertainty persist, requiring continued attention to palliative care needs. This narrative review examines palliative care in children and adolescents with advanced cystic fibrosis, focusing on multidimensional symptom burden, communication, shared decision-making, advance care planning, lung transplantation, and integration within multidisciplinary care. Building on the established longitudinal, needs-based framework for palliative care in cystic fibrosis, we examine its application specifically to paediatric care in the era of highly effective modulator therapies. Palliative care can complement disease-directed therapies throughout the disease trajectory rather than being reserved for end-of-life care. In children and adolescents, needs are shaped not only by disease severity but also by developmental stage, evolving autonomy, family circumstances, education and social participation, transplantation, and transition to adulthood. Multidisciplinary cystic fibrosis teams can provide primary palliative care within their expertise, with specialist paediatric palliative care added when needs become complex or refractory. In the era of highly effective modulator therapies, the challenge is therefore to operationalise longitudinal, needs-based palliative care for children and families across increasingly heterogeneous disease trajectories. Future research should define approaches to needs assessment, escalation of palliative support, specialist referral, and implementation within multidisciplinary cystic fibrosis services, with the aim of improving quality of life alongside longer survival.

papers.abstract_en: The reliable room-temperature (RT) detection of organophosphorus (OP) nerve agents remains a critical challenge for public safety, hindered by sluggish diffusion and poor adsorption affinity of targets like sarin (GB) and its simulant dimethyl methylphosphonate (DMMP). Here, by mimicking the structure and function of natural enzyme, we rationally designed a bioinspired, repairable hybrid architecture that achieves highly sensitive and selective RT detection of DMMP. Our design integrates a self-assembled porous L-cystine layer derived from a two-dimensional MoS2 modified with L-cysteine. This hierarchical structure uniquely enables a synergistic "recognition-enrichment-transport-sensing" cascade elucidated by comprehensive spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations: the porous layer enriches DMMP molecules and facilitates their diffusion to underlying MoS2 interface, where specific adsorption triggers significant electron transfer. The sensor demonstrates an ultra-low RT practical detection limit down to 10 ppb, along with fast response, excellent selectivity, and long-term stability. Furthermore, when integrated into a flexible wearable device, the sensor exhibits outstanding mechanical bending stability and easy repairability enabled by the reversible disulfide bonds, allowing for architectural reconstruction after damage. This work offers a promising biomimetic strategy to overcome the intrinsic limitations of OP sensing and paves the way for durable, RT-wearable detection technologies in practical security applications.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Impact assessment surveys (IAS) are central to monitoring and evaluating the effectiveness of mass drug administration (MDA) programs targeting soil-transmitted helminths (STH). Current survey designs often follow guidelines that lack flexibility and spatial representativeness. There is a need for more efficient and context-adaptable methodologies that can guide programmatic decision-making using available data. METHODS: We developed a three-step geostatistical framework for optimal IAS design that integrates baseline prevalence data, environmental covariates, and treatment history. A geostatistical model is used to estimate baseline prevalence. A Markov model, coupled with a local spatial thinning algorithm, is then applied to forecast post-MDA prevalence surfaces. These projections guide the simulation and evaluation of candidate survey designs across different sampling intensities and spatial configurations. Design performance was assessed based on classification accuracy and survey cost. RESULTS: The methodology was applied to datasets from Kenya, Sierra Leone, and Zimbabwe. Compared to conventional survey designs, our model-based approach achieved similar classification accuracy with 60-90% lower survey costs. These gains were consistent across settings with different endemicity levels and deworming histories. The results also highlight the importance of leveraging spatial correlation and historical program data to inform efficient design. CONCLUSIONS: Our approach offers a flexible and cost-effective solution for designing IAS under real-world constraints. By incorporating spatial modeling and intervention history, it enables evidence-based decision-making and resource allocation. This framework is disease-agnostic and can be adapted to other neglected tropical diseases to support progress toward control and elimination goals.

papers.abstract_en: Protein fingerprinting with nanopores enables single-molecule proteoform analysis but is often limited by conformational heterogeneity of flexible polypeptides. Here, we reduce this stochasticity through a geometric relocalization strategy by engineering dual hydrophobic anchoring sites (T83F/R118F) in the vestibule of the Mycobacterium smegmatis porin A (M2MspA) nanopore. These substitutions are proposed to create localized aromatic interaction sites that alter the docking geometry of the folded Smt3 domain and improve the reproducibility of sensing-segment presentation near the constriction. We demonstrated that this reconfiguration could convert stochastic, tail-dominated signals into regulated, segment-resolved readouts. Analysis of the single-site mutants suggests that R118F makes the predominant contribution to the observed reporter-positioning phenotype, enabling discrimination of peptide sequences unresolved in M2MspA. Using this spatial control, we achieve single-molecule detection of lysine acetylation in a tau-derived peptide via distinct noise signatures. These results support a nanopore design strategy that emphasizes spatial alignment for high-fidelity proteoform analysis.

papers.affiliation_highlight: Zhejiang Lab , Hangzhou311100, China.

papers.reason: 提供压电复合材料兼作声腔与换能器的壁主动式光声传感思路，可作为呼气气体检测与无创诊断硬件方向的早期技术参照；当前结果尚不能支撑任何胸科临床决策或科研对照。
papers.abstract_en: Compact photoacoustic trace-gas sensors require acoustic detectors that combine high sensitivity with mechanical integrability, but conventional high-performance detectors are typically rigid, discrete components that are difficult to merge with shape-adaptive acoustic architectures. Here, we report a monolithic photoacoustic CO2 sensor enabled by an interface-engineered reconfigurable piezocomposite, in which the sensing film itself can serve as both the acoustic cavity wall and the piezoelectric detector. The water-processed composite combines Cu@PZT metal-ferroelectric heterointerfaces, sparse MWCNT electrical bridges and a glucose-urea-reconstructed cellulose matrix. Surface-anchored Cu domains on PZT act as localized charge-regulation sites that mitigate polymer dielectric shielding and depolarization effects, yielding a piezoelectric coefficient of 83.2 pC N-1, while the dynamic hydrogen-bonded cellulose network provides the deformability required for conformal and tubular architectures. In a planar PAS configuration, the piezocomposite functions as a flexible acoustic detector attached to a discrete resonant cavity, giving a CO2 sensitivity of 2.92 mV ppm-1 and a detection limit of 148 ppb. When rolled into a monolithic tubular sensor, the same film forms the resonant cavity wall and performs wall-active acoustic-to-electrical transduction, increasing the sensitivity to 7.11 mV ppm-1 and lowering the detection limit to 13 ppb at a 10 s integration time, with a normalized noise equivalent absorption of 2.03 × 10-8 cm-1 W Hz-1/2. This work establishes a material-to-sensor-architecture route for wall-active photoacoustic trace-gas detection, showing how reconfigurable piezocomposites can integrate acoustic resonance and electrical detection within a single deformable sensing structure.

papers.abstract_en: Single-cell Assay for Transposase Accessible Chromatin (scATAC-seq) is increasingly used at population scale to study how genetic variation shapes chromatin accessibility. Method development is limited by the lack of flexible simulation tools with known ground truth. Here, we present simPIC, a fast, memory-efficient framework for simulating realistic single-cell ATAC-seq count data across individuals and populations. simPIC models cell groups, batch effects, and genotype-dependent accessibility variation, enabling evaluation of population-scale methods, including chromatin accessibility quantitative trait locus mapping. Across multiple datasets and cell types, simPIC closely matches real data distributions while scaling to cohort sizes impractical for current tools.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Families from underserved communities face disproportionate barriers to accessing early years support. In response, Early Years GP Child Health Hub Pilots were set up in three North West London boroughs (Brent, Ealing, Harrow) between 2023 and 2025 to improve access to integrated services, reflecting the NHS 10-Year Plan’s ambition for neighbourhood-based care. The hubs have been funded to continue supporting local communities. However, there is limited understanding of how parents from underserved communities experience these services and the challenges they encounter in engaging with them. This study explored practitioner-reported barriers parents face in accessing and engaging with integrated child health services. METHODS: We used qualitative multiple practitioner-generated case study data specifically for families with children aged 0–5 years from the three pilot sites. We applied the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation-Behaviour (COM-B) framework to analyse the data thematically, guided deductively by the framework and inductively allowing for emergent themes. RESULTS: Twenty-one case studies, collected between September 2024 and January 2025, were generated by practitioners using information they recorded from contact with each family. Barriers were identified across all COM-B domains and multiple barriers overlapping domains. Capability barriers were reported to be the most common (eg, poor parental mental health, low parenting confidence and limited health literacy). Opportunity barriers included financial hardship, competing priorities, social isolation and family interference. Motivational barriers included fear of judgement, emotional stress and previous negative experiences with services. The case studies also identified several enablers including trusted practitioner relationships, culturally sensitive care, proactive follow-up and multidisciplinary collaboration. CONCLUSION: Families living in disadvantaged areas face multiple, intersecting barriers to engaging with integrated services. Child Health Hubs should adopt co-produced, community-informed approaches with parents that integrate health and social support to improve equitable access and sustained engagement for families experiencing adversity.

papers.abstract_en: The real-time, in vivo measurement of drugs, metabolites, and biomarkers in awake animals could enable unprecedented insights into metabolic regulation, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and behavioral response. In pursuit of this vision, here we demonstrate a subcutaneous electrochemical aptamer-based (EAB) sensor architecture that (i) supports the seconds-resolved, real-time measurement of specific molecular analytes over extended periods in freely moving, normally behaving rats and (ii) we believe is easily transferrable to other researchers. The approach also enables concurrent behavioral tracking captured ambulation metrics, which can reveal correlations between the in vivo concentrations of psychoactive drugs and locomotor behavior. The results of this multimodal approach validate EAB sensors for multianalyte detection in dynamic physiological contexts and highlights the physiological and psychobiological relevance of interstitial fluid drug concentrations, with implications for precision dosing, real-time molecular diagnostics, and behavioral pharmacology.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE OF THE REVIEW: We reviewed how heat exposure is defined using thresholds and reference temperatures derived from the temperature-mortality exposure-response curve in time-series and case-crossover studies using distributed lag non-linear models and propose a harmonisation framework relevant to climate change research and heat disaster preparedness. RECENT FINDINGS: The rapid review identified variation across studies in heat thresholds and reference temperatures, affecting the comparability of estimates. A case study in Spain illustrates how the minimum mortality temperature (MMT) approach estimates overall heat-related mortality and its contributions from moderate and extreme heat, whereas the percentile-based approach estimates excessive heat mortality that could potentially be prevented by protective measures operating above the heat threshold. Differences in heat thresholds and reference temperatures make findings harder to compare across studies and complicate risk communication. Explicit reporting of these two components and their relevance to the research question and intended application would improve interpretation and translation to public health action.

papers.abstract_en: Neonatal mechanical ventilation is a cornerstone in the management of respiratory failure in newborns (NBs), particularly in preterm infants, in whom pulmonary and neurologic increases their vulnerability to ventilation-induced lung injury. At present, the primary objective of respiratory support is to ensure adequate ventilation while minimizing lung and brain injury through lung-protective strategies and careful oxygen titration. Noninvasive ventilation (NIV) is currently the first-line approach for both initial respiratory support and post-extubation care, as it reduces the need for invasive ventilation and the incidence of ventilator-induced lung injury. Multiple modalities and devices are available, and their selection should be individualized according to the underlying disease, gestational age, and clinical response. The selection of the appropriate interface and ventilatory settings and patient-ventilator synchronization are of utmost importance. Noninvasive ventilation failure should be preceded by systematic optimization and requires well-defined criteria for timely therapeutic escalation. Conventional mechanical ventilation continues to be necessary in more severe cases. Its use should be synchronized and volume-targeted whenever possible, as this strategy has been shown to reduce major complications such as pneumothorax, intraventricular hemorrhage, and the composite outcome of death or bronchopulmonary dysplasia. High-frequency oscillatory ventilation serves as a rescue strategy in refractory cases and selected clinical condition, relying on the maintenance of lung recruitment with extremely low tidal volumes. Finally, ventilatory management of the most common neonatal respiratory conditions-such as respiratory distress syndrome, meconium aspiration syndrome, air leak syndrome, and bronchopulmonary dysplasia-requires a dynamic, individualized approach focused on lung protection from the earliest hours of life.

papers.abstract_en: Developing effective nanomedicines for pulmonary metastasis remains challenging because of systemic clearance and local stromal barriers. Guided by single-cell transcriptomic profiling, we characterized a compartmentalized immunosuppressive network involving PGE2 and provide a biological rationale for coordinated EP2/EP4 antagonism. We therefore engineered an inhalable biomimetic platform (PD-1@E2/4 Exo) comprising PD-1-displaying exosomes co-loaded with EP2 and EP4 antagonists. Compared with intravenous administration, nebulized delivery increased pulmonary exposure of the engineered vesicles. Within the pulmonary tumor setting, surface PD-1 is intended to interfere with PD-1/PD-L1 signaling, while the co-delivered antagonists target the EP2/EP4 immunosuppressive axis. Treatment was associated with macrophage reprogramming, increased oxidative stress, and enhanced ICD-related responses in tumor cells. In the experimental breast-cancer lung-colonization model, the inhaled formulation reduced established pulmonary tumor burden and was accompanied by systemic immune-memory responses. These findings provide a preclinical study for integrating local pulmonary delivery with coordinated metabolic and immune modulation in breast cancer lung disease.

papers.abstract_en: AbstractInfluenza A virus (IAV) infection initiates a high-stakes competition for proteostatic control. While the host reconfigures its degradative machinery for defense, the virus simultaneously hijacks host proteostatic and degradative pathways to facilitate replication and evade immunity. Central to this conflict is the proteasomal switch, a process in which constitutive proteasome subunits (β1, β2, β5) are replaced by their inducible counterparts (β1i, β2i, β5i) to form the immunoproteasome (iP). Although iP is classically recognized for optimizing MHC class I antigen presentation, emerging evidence reveals more nuanced roles in IAV infections. This review synthesizes current knowledge on iP as an effector of host defense and target for viral subversion. We synthesize emerging evidence and propose working models detailing how IAV proteins may selectively interfere with proteasomal subunits to stabilize pro-viral factors. Furthermore, we examine the hypothesis that the iP functions alongside broader ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS), endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation (ERAD), and autophagic pathways as a proteostatic buffer to mitigate proteotoxic and oxidative stress in the infected epithelium. By evaluating how age-related proteostatic decay and viral subversion could impair cellular clearance machinery, we provide a conceptual framework for understanding how proteasomal dysregulation contributes to acute lung injury and the chronic inflammatory state termed as inflammaging. Finally, we propose a hypothesis-generating, biphasic framework for timing-dependent proteasomal modulation, contrasting preclinically supported late-stage β5i inhibition against the theoretical concept of early-stage activation to highlight translational hurdles in severe influenza.

papers.abstract_en: Deciphering structurally similar thiol analogues is vital for disease diagnosis, yet conventional one-to-one sensing strategies are intrinsically bottlenecked by signal cross-interference. Herein, we report an in situ reconstructed interfacial oxygen vacancies engineering strategy to prepare vacancy-rich Pt-CeO2 nanozymes for intelligent thiol differentiation. By combining incipient wetness impregnation with subsequent H2 reduction, isolated Pt single atoms were transformed into uniformly dispersed Pt clusters on CeO2 nanorods, simultaneously inducing abundant oxygen vacancies and dynamically coupled Pt-CeO2 interfaces. The optimized nanozyme exhibited significantly enhanced peroxidase-like catalytic activity over its single-atom state or directly deposited cluster counterparts. Crucially, the boosted catalytic kinetics significantly amplified the subtle response discrepancies among different thiols, yielding highly resolved time-dependent fingerprints. By integrating these distinct kinetic profiles with multivariate statistical analysis and predictive machine learning models, accurate differentiation of thiol species, complex multicomponent mixtures and clinical serum samples was achieved. This work not only provides insights into reconstruction-induced interfacial defect engineering but also establishes an effective framework for intelligent kinetic sensing in early disease screening.

papers.abstract_en: Nanofluidic ion gating underpins both biological signal transduction and iontronic signal processing. However, a simple and reliable mechanism that functions independently of local electrochemical conditions remains unavailable, hindering interference-free integration of artificial iontronic components with biological counterparts. Here, we present a nanofluidic device that enabled ionic gating through pervaporation-driven precipitation and rehydration-driven dissolution (PP&RD) of salt solutions within a nanochannel. Pervaporation induced local salt precipitation in the nanochannel, forming an electrical blockage that suppressed conductance (OFF state), whereas rehydration dissolved the precipitate and restored the conductance (ON state). The ionic gating device exhibited an ON-OFF conductance ratio exceeding 100, fully reversible operation performance, and robust switching across experimental conditions. By integrating two ionic gates in parallel or in series within a single device, we further implement Boolean OR and AND logic operations. PP&RD-based ionic gating thus provided a simple, versatile, and practical foundation for scalable iontronic circuit architecture.

papers.abstract_en: Non-Hermitian systems host a wealth of exotic phenomena, yet their temporal topology-particularly in time-reversal-symmetry-broken conditions-remains largely unexplored. Here, we experimentally demonstrate topological memory emerging from hysteresis-driven dynamics in a nonreciprocal microwave scattering system. The scattering singularity, encompassing both backscattering zeros and nonreciprocal exceptional points (EPs), serves as the cornerstone of this effect. Magnetic hysteresis induces a history-dependent trajectory of the complex scattering parameter that winds around such singularities, giving rise to quantized topological charges and sharp transitions when crossing them. At the limit of infinite nonreciprocity, backscattering zeros facilitate access to EPs, drastically easing their realization and yielding enhanced frequency combs near the transition. Extending these dynamics to free-space broadcasting and circulator-based topological insulators, we demonstrate nonreciprocity-assisted transport and long-distance preservation of scattering singularities. Our results uncover the interplay among singularity, nonreciprocity, and Floquet engineering, establishing a unified platform for exploring temporal topology and in-memory non-Hermitian photonics.
