papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Glioblastoma is the most aggressive and fatal primary malignant brain tumour in adults, characterised by extensive intra-tumour heterogeneity, diffuse infiltration into surrounding brain tissue. Despite advances in surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy, patient prognosis remains poor, underscoring the critical need for improved biological insight to guide precision medicine potential strategies. Although traditional bulk genomic and transcriptomic analyses have made a substantial contribution to understanding glioblastoma pathophysiology, such average molecular signals across cell populations obscures tumour microenvironment influence and clinically significant cellular states. RECENT FINDINGS: Recent advances in single-cell and spatial omics technologies have revolutionised glioblastoma research by enabling high-resolution analysis of tumour composition, cellular plasticity, and spatial organisation. These modalities have revealed that glioblastoma is composed of dynamic and plastic cellular states as opposed to fixed molecular subtypes, including stem-like and therapy-resistant populations that contribute to recurrence. The tumour architecture is preserved by spatially resolved transcriptomic and proteomic approaches, which reveal regional transcriptional programmes influenced by the tumour ecosystem. The findings provide a more resolved view of glioblastoma evolution and treatment resistance, challenging current classification systems. However, significant challenges remain in integrating these high-dimensional datasets, managing technical and computational demands, and translating these approaches into clinically scalable workflows which collectively hinder their translational adoption. This review aims to synthesise recent advances in glioblastoma single-cell and spatial omics, critically evaluating both advantages and limitations in understanding tumour heterogeneity and tumour microenvironmental interactions. Furthermore, it assesses the current challenges of glioblastoma precision medicine and evaluates the potential of these technologies to advance such approaches.

papers.abstract_en: Microplastics (MPs) pollution has emerged as a pervasive contaminant in remote environments; however, its occurrence in high-altitude snow remains poorly constrained. Here, we provide baseline evidence of MP contamination in snow from four mountaineering camps on Mount Aconcagua (6,962 masl), the highest peak in the Americas and in the entire Western and Southern Hemispheres. Microplastics were identified using µFTIR-ATR spectroscopy. The mean MPs concentration was 38 MP L-1, with site-specific values of 79 ± 37, 27 ± 8.3, 40 ± 16, and 5 ± 1 MP L-1 at the Plaza de Mulas base camp, and at the Canada, Nido de Condores, and Berlin higher elevations camps, respectively. Significantly higher concentrations at the base camp highlight the influence of intense human activity on MP accumulation, even in these remote high-mountain settings. Fibers (<5 mm), predominantly blue, were the dominant shape (90%), and polymer analysis revealed polyester, polyethylene, and epoxy as the main constituents. These findings indicate that snow is an effective matrix for assessing atmospheric deposition of MPs in andine environments. The spatial distribution of MPs suggests that local emissions associated with mountaineering activities represent a key source, although long-range atmospheric transport cannot be excluded. Our study provides the first documented evidence of the pollution of MPs in this world-famous climbing area, underscoring the vulnerability of high-altitude ecosystems to plastic pollution. Given the ecological significance and increasing human pressure in the Aconcagua Provincial Park, these results highlight the urgent need for targeted waste management strategies and regulatory actions to mitigate MP inputs in this fragile mountain environment.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cannabis is the most used illicit substance among adolescents. Regular cannabis use is linked to cognitive and psychosocial difficulties. As no pharmacological treatment has proven effective, psychological interventions, including motivational interviewing (MI), cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), and family-based approaches, remain central. However, adolescent-specific evidence remains limited. TIMCA was developed as a ten-session integrative psychotherapy combining MI, CBT, and integrated attachment therapy. While family therapy may not be indicated for all adolescents, parental involvement remains important for the adolescent-parent relationship. TIMCA therefore combines individual and parent-adolescent sessions to address cannabis use alongside attachment-related and emotion-regulation processes. OBJECTIVES: This pilot randomized controlled trial evaluated the feasibility and acceptability of TIMCA and explored changes over time in cannabis use and relational, emotional, anxiety/depressive, and treatment-adherence outcomes compared with treatment as usual (TAU). METHODS: Thirty-nine adolescents with cannabis use disorder were randomly assigned to TIMCA (n = 19) or TAU (n = 20) in two outpatient addiction services in the Paris metropolitan area. Cannabis use, attachment security, emotion regulation, anxiety, and depressive symptoms were assessed at baseline, mid-treatment, post-treatment, and 1-month follow-up using self-report measures and urine toxicology. RESULTS: TIMCA was feasible and acceptable, with high treatment adherence. Exploratory analyses showed significant within-group changes, including reductions in cannabis use, emotion dysregulation, and depressive symptoms, along with improved attachment security. In TAU, within-group changes did not reach statistical significance, and no significant between-group differences were detected. CONCLUSION: TIMCA appears feasible and acceptable, supporting further evaluation in adequately powered trials with longer follow-up.

papers.abstract_en: To address low affinity and reaction rate in monovalent ligand-aptamer binding, herein, we propose a bivalent binding-cooperated hybridization assembly (bbHA) strategy to light up the ratiometric fluorescence of convertible Ag nanoclusters (cAgNC) for detecting adenosine triphosphate (ATP). Two identical repeats of ATP-recognizable aptamer splits (a1 and a2) are separately programmed in an aptamer templating strand (aT) and an aptamer converter strand (aC), while two pairs of cAgNC-clustering and emission-converting segments are tethered in aT (template-a1-a1-template) and aC (converter-a2-a2-converter), respectively. Two tandem red cAgNC emitters are preferably developed in aT. Upon presenting ATP, the affinity recognition by a specific aptamer (a1/a2) entity enables cooperative binding events for triggering rapid complementary hybridization of aT and aC. The other proximal a1/a2 pair is bulged and merged to speed up the second ATP affinity binding. The structurally stable aT·2ATP·aC complex is formed to orient two ended converters and clusters together, thereby modulating its red fluorescence into green through electronic interactions between Ag0 and particular nucleobases. The resulting signal ratio of dual-emissive cAgNC exhibits a linear dependence on ATP, achieving sensitive and accurate quantification via inherent built-in correction. In contrast to the monovalent mechanism, the bbHA-based strategy features superior assay performances such as higher target responsiveness, faster reaction kinetics, and more efficient transduction. Thus, this label-free method would offer a new paradigm to construct simplified, specific, robust, and cost-effective sensing platforms for applicable assay of various small-molecule analytes.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: As climate-related events, such as floods and bushfires, become more frequent and severe, it is increasingly important to understand health consumers' needs during these crises. This study explored the lived experiences of Australians who managed a health condition-either their own or as a carer-during climate events. METHODS: In-depth, one-on-one online interviews were conducted with 20 participants aged 18-80 years living with a range of chronic and acute health conditions. Findings were analysed using inductive thematic analysis. RESULTS: Participants faced challenges, including the exacerbation of existing and newly developed health conditions, disruptions to healthcare services and the home environment, as well as knowledge or information barriers, that complicated health condition management. Participants adopted various strategies for these challenges, including self-management practices, accessing social support, leveraging communication channels, and seeking alternative care pathways. CONCLUSIONS: Clear, accessible communication and consumer preparedness support are critical for maintaining care continuity during climate events. Developing system-level contingency plans for alternative care could ensure care continuity. While digital tools can facilitate access to information, their availability could be limited when infrastructure is disrupted.

papers.abstract_en: Targeting interleukin (IL) signaling has long been constrained by the extensive, topologically flat and dynamic nature of cytokine-receptor interfaces. While monoclonal antibodies have validated these pathways clinically, achieving comparable efficacy with small molecules or non-antibody modalities demands overcoming steep pharmacokinetic and structural hurdles. In this review, we examine the translational trajectory across IL-17, IL-23, IL-1-family and IL-6 pathways-tracing compounds from in silico and biophysical hit identification to cellular and clinical validation. Rather than focusing merely on surface binding, we dissect the interplay between pocket dynamics (cryptic sites), modality selection (orally bioavailable macrocycles and traditional Rule-of-Five chemotypes) and the systemic liabilities of pathway crosstalk. These case studies provide pragmatic frameworks for converting structural ligandability into durable clinical outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: The 2026 outbreak of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), involved limited international exportation but remained centred in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The outbreak tested whether earlier institutional mobilisation translated into timely field delivery. We conducted a structured narrative review of peer-reviewed research, official reports and operational guidance on epidemiology, diagnostics, medical countermeasures (MCMs), One Health surveillance, clinical care, infection prevention and control (IPC), community engagement and cross-border preparedness. Key institutional mechanisms for emergency decision-making, coordination and MCM prioritisation were activated earlier than during the 2013-2016 Ebola virus disease epidemic in West Africa, widening the window for action. Field delivery nevertheless remained uneven: the model-adjusted median onset-to-sampling delay was 4.8 days among 129 confirmed patients, while insecurity posed additional challenges for field response. Preparedness was further constrained by uncertainty about reservoir ecology, limited clinical validation of BDBV-specific diagnostics and the absence of MCMs with established efficacy in BVD. We therefore propose a One Health alert-to-action pathway linking human, animal, environmental and community signals to BDBV-inclusive confirmation, safe care, IPC, cross-border continuity, accountable governance and feedback-informed adaptation. Earlier activation is a preparedness gain, but protection depends on whether that advantage is carried through reliable, traceable and equitable operational hand-offs.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Socially interactive AI can elicit meaningful relational experiences. Studies often conflate attachment, anthropomorphism, companionship, dependence, and addiction, and group embodied robots with dissimilar software. METHODS: This critical narrative review of a reconstructed, non-exhaustive corpus (Grant & Booth, 2009) is interpretive, not aggregative, because the initial search records disagree. We rebuilt the evidence set from the initially identified literature, separated primary from contextual sources, and sorted them by embodiment and dialogue architecture. Coding kept attachment functions distinct from related constructs. A reproducible OpenAlex and PubMed search (2010-2025) retrieved only one of the 12 primary reports. A coverage probe found 34 further provisionally eligible reports. We claim no exhaustive coverage or full PRISMA compliance. RESULTS: Reclassification left 12 primary reports and seven contextual sources. In these reports, relational significance appeared with embodied robots, non-LLM systems, and generative systems, carried by co-presence and touch or by conversational contingency, personalisation, and apparent continuity. Most measured companionship, trust, social presence, perceived support, or one problematic-use indicator. Few covered more than one attachment-system function. None established a behavioural-addiction syndrome. The predominantly cross-sectional, self-selected evidence cannot establish whether heavier use causes loneliness. CONCLUSIONS: A relationship with an AI system can matter without amounting to reciprocal human attachment or behavioural addiction. Within the reviewed corpus, the evidence supports a broad, uneven continuum of involvement. Omitted studies may change the apparent mix of constructs, technologies, and outcomes. Progress requires longitudinal, technology-stratified studies with construct-specific measures that establish temporal order and impairment and separate embodiment from generative capability.

papers.abstract_en: Despite major scientific advances, pharmaceutical R&D productivity remains a persistent challenge. This study motivates a network-centric model in which R&D performance can depend not only on firm-level scientific capabilities, but also increasingly on effective positioning and orchestration within innovation networks. Bibliometric analysis showed that previously reported network reconfiguration during the mid-2010s was temporally aligned with the rise of precision medicine. Approval-based analysis revealed the growing contribution of spin-offs and changing roles of large pharmaceutical companies, particularly for new modalities. An exploratory case analysis revealed distinct strategic trajectories in two spin-offs developing conventional or new modality products. Together, these observations converge to suggest strategic implications for pharmaceutical companies, investors, and policymakers navigating the era of precision medicine and new modalities.

papers.abstract_en: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) plays a crucial role in environmental remediation, chemical synthesis, and energy storage. Nevertheless, its industrial production is energy consuming with significant environmental burdens. Here we show a proof-of-concept thermoelectrocatalytic strategy for H2O2 production directly from seawater, driven solely by low-grade waste heat. A low-temperature thermoelectric (TE) material, Na- and Pb-codoped SnSe, is designed as a catalyst that enables efficient H2O2 generation under a moderate temperature gradient (ΔT). This system achieves an H2O2 production rate of 6.1 mmol g-1 h-1 from seawater under ΔT = 120 K, which is competitive with the representative photocatalytic systems. Experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that Na/Pb-codoping improves the TE properties, promotes charge carrier migration under ΔT, and promotes the oxygen reduction reaction toward H2O2 formation. The naturally formed strong electric layer at the catalyst-seawater interface further promotes both reaction kinetics and thermodynamic driving forces. Our finding provides a sustainable route for H2O2 production from seawater using waste heat and demonstrates great potential of TE-catalysis for waste heat utilization.

papers.abstract_en: Methadone is a long-standing synthetic opioid that remains clinically important for pain management and opioid use disorder, yet it exemplifies the dual nature of opioid drug discovery. Despite its therapeutic success, methadone exhibits complex pharmacokinetics, polypharmacology and safety liabilities that have limited its broader clinical application. This review examines methadone as a case study to illustrate how chemical structure, stereochemistry, receptor pharmacology and pharmacokinetic properties collectively shape therapeutic outcomes and risk. We summarize key advances in methadone synthesis, structure-activity relationships, pharmacology and clinical limitations and discuss how lessons learned from methadone continue to inform modern opioid drug discovery. Particular emphasis is placed on balancing efficacy, duration of action and safety in the design of next-generation opioid therapeutics.

papers.authors_conclusion: 健康新生儿、婴儿与儿童的止血系统并非发育不足，而是针对其生理情境被精确设计和校准；年龄特异性参考区间变化与功能性代偿机制支持“儿科止血是发育适应的生理学范本”这一观点；作者批判“immature”等过时术语，指出误标在儿童血栓与止血领域的下游后果，并呼吁修订术语体系以更准确反映发育中止血系统的功能复杂性。

papers.abstract_en: The hemostatic system of neonates, infants, and children has historically and recently been described using the term "immature", a label that implies deficiency, incompleteness, or even developmental failure. We challenge that characterization. Drawing on more than three decades of advances in developmental hemostasis, we argue that the hemostatic system of healthy newborns, infants, and children is not underdeveloped, but rather precisely designed and calibrated for its physiological context. Age-specific changes reflected in reference ranges, and functional compensatory mechanisms, support the view that pediatric hemostasis represents a physiological masterclass in developmental adaptation, not an imperfect approximation of adult function. We examine the historical trajectory of this field, critique the use of outdated terminology, identify key conceptual gaps, and discuss the downstream consequences of mislabeling in the context of pediatric thrombosis and hemostasis. We conclude with a call for a revised lexicon that more accurately reflects the functional sophistication of the developing hemostatic system.

papers.abstract_en: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of mortality and disability worldwide. Disulfide-bond oxidized HMGB1 (ds-HMGB1) functions as a core damage-associated molecular pattern that mediates acute myocardial injury. Nevertheless, commercially available HMGB1 reagents exhibit mixed proteoforms, unstable biological activity and low receptor affinity, which greatly hinder mechanistic investigations in this field. This study generated a novel mutant full-length murine ds-HMGB1, systematically dissected its molecular mechanisms underlying aggravated ischemic myocardial injury, and sought to provide a standardized protein reagent and theoretical framework for HMGB1-targeted therapies against myocardial damage. A K184S/K185S mutant HMGB1 plasmid was constructed, and protein purified by three-step chromatography. Structural modeling, mass spectrometry, SPR and PLA were used to analyze conformation, modification and receptor binding kinetics. Hypoxic cardiomyocyte co-culture and mouse myocardial infarction models were established. Flow cytometry, echocardiography, histological staining, qPCR, Western blot and RNA-seq were applied to detect molecular phenotypes and signaling pathways. The K184S/K185S mutation preserved the native overall conformation and functional disulfide bond of HMGB1, while markedly enhancing HMGB1 binding to RAGE and promoting TLR4-MD2 complex assembly. In vitro experiments revealed that mutant ds-HMGB1 either acted directly on cardiomyocytes or synergized hypoxia through endothelial-cardiomyocyte paracrine signaling to induce robust intracellular ROS accumulation, mitochondrial dysfunction and cardiomyocyte apoptosis. In vivo administration expanded myocardial infarct size, impaired cardiac systolic performance and exacerbated inflammatory infiltration in cardiac tissue. Transcriptomic profiling identified 53 core injury genes specifically upregulated by ds-HMGB1 under ischemic stress. The mutant ds-HMGB1 developed in this study addresses the intrinsic drawbacks of commercial HMGB1 preparations. We further identified 53 key myocardial injury genes modulated by ds-HMGB1. This work delivers a standardized experimental reagent and multi-layered mechanistic evidence supporting HMGB1 as a therapeutic target for acute myocardial infarction.

papers.authors: Gu C, Zhai Z, Ding S, Han C, Zhang T, Xiang C

papers.abstract_en: Direct photolithography offers a transformative photoresist-free route for high-precision integration in electronic and optoelectronic platforms. Despite significant advancements in quantum dots (QDs), existing methods often degrade optoelectronic performance due to the inherent surface ligand changes during photolithographic processing. Here, we introduce a reversible photolithography strategy to overcome this bottleneck. This strategy is based on the first wavelength-gated, reversible ligand crosslinking and decrosslinking cycle, enabling the dynamic and reversible control over the photolithographic process. Using this approach, we achieve high-efficient and high-fidelity QD photolithography with restored QD structure and functionality. The reversible process further enables high-performance electroluminescence, with one of the highest luminance values of 125,016 cd m-2 at 5.0 V and a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 24.41%. Moreover, we demonstrate an ultrahigh-resolution nano-pixelated device with a peak EQE of 17.08% at 21,000 PPI. This work presents a photo-reversible crosslinking system that decouples photolithographic patterning from performance degradation, offering a versatile platform for high-end QD-based displays and other advanced optoelectronics.

papers.abstract_en: Simultaneously monitoring ammonia (NH3) leakage and human motion is desirable for safeguarding astronauts' safety in spacecraft equipped with NH3-driven propulsion, in which stable and selective NH3 sensing combined with reliable pressure detection is highly required. However, little is reported on a sensing material that synergistically presents the required NH3 and pressure sensing. Here, wearable NH3 and pressure sensing has been developed using PANI-wrapping carbon-intermixed Fe2O3 hierarchical microarchitectures (PANI@C-Fe2O3 HMAs), which have been synthesized by employing fern-shaped C-Fe2O3 HMAs with trunk/branches as structural precursors, followed by conformal PANI-wrapping. Beneficially, PANI@C-Fe2O3 HMAs present a wide detection range of 0.1 ppm-10 v/v%, 167-day-long stability and high selectivity toward NH3. Further, a pressure sensor prototype has been constructed by laminating PET tapes onto the HMAs-integrated flexible electrode, revealing an excellent pressure-dependent response and machine-learning-assisted human-motion recognition. Such superior dual sensing is attributed to the texturing behavior, in which conformal texturing of PANI along the hierarchical surface of C-Fe2O3 HMAs establishes heterojunctions with a built-in electric field to amplify resistance modulation, while fern-shaped HMAs with trunk/branches provide abundant active interfaces and electron transport pathways. Practically, a wearable dual-sensing device that integrates flexible NH3 and pressure sensor prototypes has been built with reliable dual-sensing responses.

papers.title_en: The genotoxic burden of toxic metals: bridging molecular mechanisms, biomonitoring, and multidisciplinary interventions.
papers.authors: Imthiaz SR, Ray S, Francis GA, Vashishth R
papers.affiliation_highlight: School of Biosciences and Technology, Vellore Institute of Technology, Vellore, India.
papers.authors_conclusion: 本综述综合了有毒金属基因毒性的现有知识及治疗策略，为研究者、医疗专业人员和政策制定者提供见解，并强调持续研究的重要性。

papers.abstract_en: We review the genotoxic effects of trace metal exposure and evaluate an efficient treatment strategy. Toxic metal(loid)s cause significant risks to animal health and ecosystems because of their toxicity and bioaccumulation potential. We then examine the mechanisms of genotoxicity, which include direct DNA damage, oxidative stress, epigenetic alterations, and interference with DNA repair mechanisms. This review highlights the health implications of toxic metal exposure: symptoms like increased cancer risks, reproductive and developmental toxicity, and chronic health disorders. Various assessment and biomonitoring techniques for toxic metal genotoxicity, including biomarkers like DNA adducts and chromosomal aberrations, and analytical methods such as the comet assay and PCR-based molecular assays, are discussed. We evaluate treatment strategies, including chelation therapy, antioxidant supplementation, and phytoremediation, emphasizing their efficacy and limitations. The importance of regulatory frameworks, public health interventions, and environmental remediation programs in mitigating toxic metal exposure is also discussed. We identify research gaps in understanding the long-term effects of low-dose chronic exposure and interactions between multiple toxic metals. This comprehensive review contributes to the field by synthesizing current knowledge on toxic metal genotoxicity and treatment strategies. We provide valuable insights for researchers, healthcare professionals, and policymakers toward the development of more effective prevention and intervention strategies. We emphasize challenges and future directions and highlight the importance of continued research in this critical area of public health and environmental science.

papers.abstract_en: We have developed a trilayered nanofiber composite (KTP) via successive electrospinning, engineered with hydrophilicity gradients supporting rapid hemostasis and wound healing. The innermost hydrophilic keratin-PVA layer initiated clotting, middle TEOS-PVA coaxial layer enhanced hemostatic efficacy, and outer PVDF layer provided protective barrier. KTP showed robust mechanical strength, cyto- and hemocompatibility, and supported cell migration. It triggered both intrinsic and extrinsic coagulation pathways and enabled platelet- and RBC-independent plasma clotting. Consistent with this, KTP upregulates tissue factor (TF) and modulates factor XII (FXII) levels in contact with plasma, indicating coordinated activation of extrinsic and contact pathways. Fibrinogen adsorption and fibrin clot stabilization occurred within 2 min, surpassing commercial dressings. Molecular docking revealed keratin's binding with coagulation proteins, which supports its mechanistic role in blood clotting. FE-SEM confirmed platelet adhesion and RBC entrapment; immunofluorescence imaging showed strong CD62P and vinculin expression, indicating active platelet engagement. In vivo injury models demonstrated rapid and stable clot formation within 35-40 s. KTP also accelerated tissue repair fully closing wounds by day 10, with complete re-epithelialization and hair follicle regeneration by day 12. Overall, this functionally graded nanofiber patch demonstrates strong potential for rapid hemorrhage control and accelerated wound healing for trauma care.

papers.abstract_en: Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (GIOP) involves impaired bone remodeling, intestinal dysbiosis, and immune imbalance, which together limit the long-term benefit of conventional oral bisphosphonate therapy. Here, we report LpEVs@ALN, a probiotic extracellular vesicle-based oral nanoplatform constructed by loading alendronate (ALN) into Lacticaseibacillus paracasei-derived extracellular vesicles. LpEVs@ALN maintains vesicle integrity and epithelial compatibility, improves ALN retention under acidic exposure, and enables sustained ALN release at intestinal pH conditions. In dexamethasone-suppressed BMSCs, LpEVs@ALN enhances osteogenic differentiation, as evidenced by increased ALP activity and matrix mineralization. In zebrafish GIOP models, LpEVs@ALN improves cranial mineralization, new bone formation, scale regeneration, and locomotor/shoaling performance; accompanied by reduced inflammatory tone, improved ALP/RANKL-associated bone turnover readouts, and rebalanced oxidative-stress indices. Microbiome profiling shows recovery of richness/diversity and reduced Proteobacteria dominance, while scale RNA-seq reveals broad reversal of glucocorticoid-driven dysregulation toward pro-osteogenic and anti-inflammatory programs. Integrated correlation analysis further linked microbial remodeling with systemic and skeletal responses, suggesting involvement of the gut-immune-bone axis. Collectively, LpEVs@ALN alleviates GIOP by combining ALN-mediated bone protection with probiotic extracellular vesicle-associated regulation of intestinal and systemic homeostasis, highlighting its potential as an oral therapeutic strategy for GIOP.

papers.abstract_en: Bacterial-fungal consortia (BFC) consistently outperform aseptic or single-species cultures in producing high-value secondary metabolites, yet the underlying cross-kingdom interaction mechanisms remain poorly understood. In food fermentations, BFCs enhance process robustness, substrate turnover, and bioactive profiles for sustainable functional foods. In these consortia, bacteria and fungi engage in complex cooperative and competitive interactions, involving signaling molecules, genetic regulation, and metabolic flux redistribution to enhance secondary metabolite yields. Based on the ecological compatibility and molecular communication mechanisms, a synthetic microbiology framework for constructing high-yield BFCs was proposed. This systematic approach included selecting appropriate coculture partners, setting up the BFC, and optimizing cultivation conditions. Functional BFCs can be effectively applied to: food fermentation, improving fermentation efficiency, nutritional value, flavor complexity, and food safety. The review provides an overview of BFCs for secondary metabolite production, with emphasis on their cross-kingdom communication mechanisms. It explores the construction and optimization of BFCs and their applications in food fermentation, identifying future directions for enhancing secondary metabolite yields.

papers.abstract_en: Malaria and neglected tropical diseases (NTDs) affect over 1 billion people worldwide. Both disease categories share overlapping geographical regions, dependence on broad-spectrum treatments and common vectors, justifying their co-consideration as a unified therapeutic challenge. We evaluate aptamers developed for malaria and NTDs, classify them into direct and delivery therapeutics and map candidates by preclinical validation stage, thereby constructing a translational road map that positions aptamers as a structurally adaptable platform addressing unmet treatment needs.

These are a broad class of secondary metabolites that are primarily synthesized by esterifying quinic acids and hydroxycinnamic acids (ferulic acid, p-coumaric acid, and caffeic acid). The most common and significant of these in the human diet is chlorogenic acid, also known as 5-O-caffeoylquinic acid (5-CQA). In addition, plants have been found to contain mono-, di-, tri-, and tetra-esters. CQAs exhibit a wide range of biological activities, including anti-inflammatory, anti-cancer, neuroprotective, antiviral, antibacterial, antiparasitic, and antidiabetic effects. In addition to their dietary significance, CQAs are used extensively in pharmacology, animal husbandry, food preservation, and the manufacturing of skin care products. CQA accumulation varies greatly across several species, plant parts, and organs. As a result, in vitro cell and organ culture techniques have been used by researchers to produce CQAs. In a variety of plant species, callus, cells, adventitious/hairy roots, and plantlet cultures have been established. In these culture types, several techniques, including cell line selection, appropriate media, salt strength, plant growth regulators, chemical and physical variables, and elicitation, have been successfully assessed.

papers.abstract_en: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) remains the leading cause of death worldwide, and many current drugs and devices are limited by off-target exposure, weak responsiveness to pathological cues, and reduced performance under pulsatile blood flow. Biomolecule-assembled materials, constructed from nucleic acids, proteins/peptides, polysaccharides, and lipids/vesicles, offer a promising way to address these limitations. Their functions arise from sequence- or chemistry-governed assembly rules that encode molecular recognition, transport, and mechanical behavior across multiple scales, from nanostructures to tissue-facing interfaces. This review summarizes recent progress in biomolecule-assembled materials across CVD prevention, diagnosis, therapy, and regeneration. Programmable bio-assemblies support rapid sensing and lesion-localized intervention, while also enabling bioactive coatings, injectable depots, and membrane-mimetic carriers for plaque targeting and drug delivery. By comparing material classes through shared cardiovascular tasks and hemodynamic constraints, modular hybrids suggest potential advantages that merit further investigation under physiologically relevant conditions. Clinical translation will depend on predictive assembly design, standardized manufacturing and quality control, and in vivo validation under physiologically relevant flow. Through converting molecular assembly rules into scalable, hemodynamically robust functions, biomolecule-assembled materials offer a unifying design language for next-generation cardiovascular diagnosis and therapy.

papers.abstract_en: Neuropathy target esterase (NTE), localized predominantly to the endoplasmic reticulum, is highly expressed within the nervous system. Under physiological conditions, NTE functions mainly as a phospholipase B/lysophospholipase involved in phosphatidylcholine and lysophosphatidylcholine turnover, thereby maintaining phospholipid homeostasis, membrane integrity, and axonal stability. In toxicology, NTE is of particular interest as the principal molecular target in organophosphorus-induced delayed neurotoxicity (OPIDN), a syndrome that develops days to weeks after exposure to certain organophosphorus (OP) compounds. Unlike acute cholinergic toxicity caused by acetylcholinesterase inhibition, OPIDN is initiated by inhibition of NTE followed by "aging" of the enzyme-inhibitor complex, an essentially irreversible process considered critical for neuropathic outcome. The resulting loss of NTE activity disrupts phospholipid metabolism, promotes lysophospholipid accumulation, endoplasmic reticulum stress, calcium dyshomeostasis, and cytoskeletal breakdown, leading to distal axon degeneration in both the central and peripheral nervous systems. Clinically, OPIDN manifests after a latent phase with progressive weakness, sensory abnormalities, gait impairment, and in severe cases persistent spasticity or paralysis. This review summarizes the current knowledge on NTE structure, catalytic function, tissue distribution, and physiological significance, and integrates these findings with the molecular and clinical features of OPIDN. Particular attention is paid to the distinction between aging (neuropathic) and non-aging (non-neuropathic) NTE inhibitors, the structural determinants of neuropathic potential, and its clinical implications.

papers.abstract_en: Ophthalmic engineering is defined by a rigorous set of constraints including the need for absolute optical clarity, precise viscoelasticity, and the ability to navigate formidable physiological barriers. Polymeric hydrogels have ascended as the quintessential material class to resolve these conflicts by leveraging their high content of water to create a seamless interface with native ocular tissues. This review critically examines the transition of these materials from passive structural substitutes to dynamic and stimulus-responsive systems. The molecular strategies required to balance mechanical robustness with biodegradation are dissected alongside the integration of responsive moieties that react to physiological cues. These principles are explored through cutting-edge clinical applications including suprachoroidal drug depots, bio-integrative tissue sealants, and closed-loop biosensing contact lenses. Finally, the discussion addresses the translational gap separating laboratory innovation from industrial manufacturing. By identifying persistent hurdles such as the inherent trade-off between long-term stability and transparency as well as sterilization compatibility, a strategic roadmap is outlined for the next generation of vision-restoring technologies.

papers.abstract_en: Brain-computer interface (BCI) provides a direct communication pathway between the brain and external devices and has been applied in neurological disease treatment, motor rehabilitation, and human-computer interaction. Electrodes play essential roles in recording and modulating neural signals, and their performance directly affects signal quality, spatial resolution, and long-term stability. Traditional rigid electrodes suffer from mechanical mismatch with brain tissue, which may induce tissue damage and reduce recording stability during long-term implantation. Flexible electrodes offer improved mechanical compatibility and have emerged as promising alternatives. Recent advances in materials science, micro/nanofabrication, and interface engineering have enhanced the electrical, mechanical, and biological performance of flexible BCI electrodes. This review summarizes neural signal characteristics, electrode requirements, fabrication strategies, and performance optimization approaches. The major fabrication methods include microelectromechanical systems (MEMS), printing and transfer, laser processing and thermal drawing, and electrospinning, while deposition and surface modification are discussed as functional enhancement strategies. The review also highlights challenges associated with large-scale manufacturing, long-term stability, and the physical and clinical limitations of invasive, semi-invasive, and noninvasive electrodes. Future directions involving intelligent, wireless, and self-powered systems, together with clinical translation, are discussed to promote the development of flexible electrodes for BCI applications.
